92dda7f48c88d1a8: GUA MUSANG: Six people, including a family of four, are feared missing after joining the Trans Gerah Expedition at Gunung Gerah in the Lojing Permanent Forest Reserve here.
The group, comprising a married couple, their two children, and two mountain guides, began their trek on Aug 29.
They were expected to arrive at Pos Kemar in Perak on Thursday, but have remained unreachable.
A source said the last contact with one of the hikers was on the morning of Sept 1, when the family reported that they were safe and healthy.
"However, they could not be contacted after that, prompting a police report to be lodged over concerns for their safety," the source said.
District police chief Superintendent Sik Choon Foo confirmed receiving the report.
"We received a report on the incident and are in touch with other agencies, including the Forestry Department.
"The group has likely crossed the Kelantan border towards Pos Kemar," he said.
0d2d33e3ed062497: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and Indonesia are strengthening intelligence-sharing and joint enforcement efforts as drug syndicates increasingly operate across borders and employ more complex methods to evade the authorities.

The matter was among the key issues discussed at the 14th bilateral meeting between Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) and the Indonesian National Police's Directorate of Narcotics Crime (Dittipidnarkoba), Bareskrim Polri, held in Genting Highlands from Sept 2 to 4.
NCID director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan chaired the Malaysian delegation, while the Indonesian delegation was led by Dittipidnarkoba director Brigadier-General Eko Hadi Santoso.
Hussein said the meeting provided both sides with an opportunity to share their experiences in tackling drug trafficking and compare notes on syndicates with links to Malaysia and Indonesia.
"We also renewed our commitment to intelligence-sharing between both sides.
"Both Malaysia and Indonesia acknowledge the importance of working closely together and sharing information, especially when dealing with syndicates whose activities cross our borders.
"Drug syndicates do not operate within the boundaries of one country, so close cooperation and the swift exchange of intelligence are important in allowing us to take action against them," he said.
Hussein said both sides also shared updates on the investigation involving the Malaysian airline second officer arrested at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport on July 29.
"We shared the progress of the co-pilot case with our Indonesian counterparts and also expressed our appreciation for their swift action and the sharing of information with us.

"This case is an example of why cooperation between enforcement agencies from both countries is important. Information obtained and shared between both sides has allowed us to further develop our investigations," he said.

Police said the bilateral meeting also focused on strategic issues and the latest developments in regional drug trafficking, including the exchange of information on emerging trends and syndicate modus operandi.
Both sides discussed strengthening cooperation in operations and investigations, as well as efforts to dismantle increasingly complex and dynamic cross-border drug distribution networks.
The meeting comes amid continued cooperation between Malaysian and Indonesian narcotics authorities in tackling syndicates operating between the two countries.
Most recently, an NCID team was sent to Jakarta from Aug 11 to 15 to assist investigations into the Malaysian second officer arrested at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport.
Information obtained during the team's visit subsequently led NCID to arrest six local men, aged between 23 and 50, in Malaysia between Aug 20 and 28.
Hussein had said the six were believed to have supplied and transported drugs for the 39-year-old second officer and played "upline" and "downline" roles in the distribution network.
The bilateral meeting also sought to strengthen institutional ties between NCID and Dittipidnarkoba, with a welcoming dinner held on Sept 2 and a gala dinner the following day.

Malaysia's delegation included NCID deputy directors Deputy Commissioner Mohd Zani Che Din and Senior Assistant Commissioner Datuk Zairulnizam Mohd Zainuddin @ Hilmi, as well as senior intelligence, operations, investigation and international liaison officers.
759577ba02cf3d03: SERDANG, Sept 6 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said he spoke with former US vice-president Al Gore about the global climate crisis, haze affecting Malaysia and the country’s transition towards cleaner energy.
Anwar said Gore, who was in Singapore, had expressed sympathy over the haze after the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading in Serian, Sarawak exceeded 500 two days ago.

“Former US vice-president Al Gore was in Singapore, and I had the opportunity to have a lengthy discussion with him about the environment and what is now referred to as the climate crisis,” he said in his speech at the closing ceremony of the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Exhibition here today.
Anwar said they also discussed the wider effects of climate change, including the recent floods in Nepal.
“Glacier ice from the Himalayan mountain range, which had remained firmly intact for thousands of years, melted into a massive valley in Nepal.
“This affects not only the people of Nepal, but also the people of Malaysia,” he said.

He said their discussion also touched on Malaysia’s commitment and ongoing efforts to accelerate the country’s energy transition away from fossil fuels towards cleaner and more sustainable energy sources.
“These are matters we cannot afford to forget; however, what we are capable of planning, we must execute,” Anwar said.
He also invited Gore to visit Malaysia soon to continue their discussions and explore closer cooperation on climate change and the country’s energy transition.
Gore, a prominent climate campaigner and founder and chairman of The Climate Reality Project, served as US vice-president from 1993 to 2001.
Anwar and Gore’s association dates back to 1998, when the American was US vice-president and Anwar was deputy prime minister before his dismissal from government and subsequent arrest.

During the 1998 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Kuala Lumpur, Gore publicly praised Malaysia’s reformasi movement, which had emerged following Anwar’s removal from office, prompting an angry response from the government of then-prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad.
Separately, Anwar said he had declined an opportunity to meet former Indonesian president Joko Widodo, who is currently in Penang, due to his prior commitments in Kuala Lumpur today.
7154a4984ac05e57: BEIRUT: Lebanon said four people were killed on Sunday in strikes which Israel said it carried out after Hezbollah had launched drones at its soldiers in south Lebanon, the latest escalation amid a fragile truce.
Lebanon's health ministry reported two people killed in south Lebanon's Nabatieh al-Fawqa and two women killed in nearby Arab Salim.

It said 20 other people including several women and three children were wounded in those locations as well as in the city of Nabatieh and the town of Kfar Rumman, adding that the toll was provisional.
Israel's army said it was striking south Lebanon after Hezbollah fighters launched two drones towards Israeli soldiers operating in Israel's self-declared "security zone" in the south.
It slammed a "blatant violation" by Hezbollah, without reporting troop casualties in the incident.

Shortly before the statement, Israel's military had issued its first evacuation notice in Lebanon in several weeks, warning residents near a building it identified as a Hezbollah "facility" in Arab Salim to evacuate ahead of an attack on the site.
It did not issue warnings for other areas where strikes were reported.
Lebanon's state-run National News Agency (NNA) said that after the Israeli warning for the building, "enemy warplanes launched a strike on another house, destroying it" and killing the two women.
It said the Israeli military subsequently "carried out a strike on the home" threatened in the evacuation warning.
'Security zone'
The NNA said a strike in Nabatieh al-Fawqa destroyed part of the Ghandour hospital, adding that it had been out of service for years.

It also said a heavy airstrike on Nabatieh city targeted a historical building and damaged offices belonging to state finance and agriculture authorities, while shops and cafes in the vicinity were also damaged.
It also reported a strike on a motorcycle in the area.
Lebanon was drawn into the Middle East war in March after Hezbollah attacked Israel in support of its backer Iran.
Israel responded with airstrikes and a ground invasion that Lebanon says have killed more than 4,300 people.
Israeli forces are still operating inside a self-declared "security zone" around 10km deep inside Lebanon along the border.
Violence has lessened since a US-Iran memorandum of understanding on the broader conflict in June, while Israel and Lebanon signed a framework agreement later that month.
However, Lebanon still reports Israeli strikes, artillery shelling and broad demolitions of civilian buildings in southern villages and towns.

On Friday, Israeli strikes in the country's south and east killed four people including an 18-year-old woman, authorities said, as Israel said it struck Hezbollah targets in response to a drone launch towards its soldiers.
Earlier this week, Israel said it had taken "operational control" of the strategic Ali al-Taher ridge near Nabatieh.
Hezbollah has not commented on the announcement or confirmed that Israel has captured the site.
Also this week, the International Committee of the Red Cross facilitated the transfer to Lebanon of five people detained by Israel.
Israel and Lebanon began direct negotiations after the latest hostilities erupted, with fresh talks expected this month, though no date has been announced.
fafea084e6eb9337: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek has praised Taanusiya Chetty, who finished third in the Miss World 2026 pageant, for championing education and advocacy as part of her cause.
“I am impressed not only by her achievement on the world stage, but also by Taanusiya’s commitment to making education and advocacy part of her cause.
“Beauty may open the door to the stage, but knowledge and critical thinking determine what we do once we are on it.
“Congratulations, Taanusiya. Continue to use the platform and voice you have to champion meaningful causes. Malaysia is proud!” she said in a Facebook post today.
In last night’s ceremony in Nha Trang, Vietnam, Joheirry Mola Dominguez of the Dominican Republic was crowned Miss World 2026, while Elisabeth Reynes Alabern of Spain finished second.

Taanusiya, 26, finished among the top three after delivering impressive and consistent performances throughout the nearly month-long competition, overcoming the challenge of 110 other contestants from around the world.

The achievement matches the record set by Lina Teoh, who also finished third at Miss World 1998, making the two Malaysian representatives the country’s best-performing contestants in the history of the contest.

Taanusiya, better known as Taanu, qualified for the Top Six after winning the Beauty With A Purpose (BWAP) segment, one of the major Miss World recognitions, awarded based on the contestants’ commitment to and impact of the community projects they champion. — Bernama

597abb9d95dc552d: KUALA LUMPUR: Independent mixed doubles pair Hoo Pang Ron-Lai Pei Jing have set their sights on qualifying for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics following an encouraging campaign at the China Masters.
The world No. 85 finished runners-up after losing 21-19, 21-16 to China's world No. 1 Feng Yan Zhe-Huang Dong Ping in the mixed doubles final at the Shenzhen Arena today.
The defeat saw them miss the opportunity to become the first Malaysian mixed doubles pair to win a Super 750 tournament.
However, the result has strengthened Pang Ron-Pei Jing's belief in a partnership that began only this year.
The qualifying period for LA28 will run from May 3 next year until April 30, 2028.
"Of course, we are looking forward to fighting for the Olympics. That's our goal," said Pang Ron.
"We will take it step by step, but we don't want to put too much pressure on ourselves. Most importantly, we want to enjoy the game."
Pang Ron admitted nerves prevented them from producing their best badminton in the opening exchanges.
"I don't feel we were at our best. Maybe we were a little too nervous," he said.
"But after playing a few points, we became used to the environment and got better and better."
Pei Jing was satisfied with their overall performance in Shenzhen, especially their ability to recover whenever doubts crept in.
"I'm happy with our overall performance here," said Pei Jing.
"Even when we faced negative thoughts, we tried to regain our focus."

The China Masters was their eighth tournament together, and Pei Jing believes she has found the right partner after trying several combinations following Tan Kian Meng's retirement earlier in the year.
"Every partner has different strengths, but now I am focused on Pang Ron and myself," she said.
"I think it is really working out."

1306440e54e64599: KUALA LUMPUR: The eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau, which spewed volcanic ash across parts of Indonesia, has disrupted flight operations, particularly at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport in Tangerang, Banten.
Several passengers, including Malaysians, shared their experiences online after being stranded while attempting to return home.
Among them was Threads user Spritzerphilips, who was stuck at the airport when her scheduled flight was affected today.
"I'm stranded in Indonesia and can't get back to Malaysia. I asked the Malaysian Embassy here in Jakarta for help, but they said there was nothing they could do.
"I'm trying to find a hotel, but many are already fully booked," she said.
An hour later, Spritzerphilips said she managed to secure a new flight on Tuesday.

"I've found a hotel and my flight has also been rescheduled for Tuesday. If it's still cancelled on Tuesday, I'll travel to Yogyakarta, as suggested by people on Threads. At least I can make alternative plans if I get stranded again," she said.
Other social media users suggested she travel by land to Yogyakarta or Surabaya to catch a flight back to Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA).
Meanwhile, Facebook user Muhamad Norshahrizal Norizan said he and his family had been stranded in Jakarta for two days following repeated flight cancellations.
"Our flight has been cancelled for two days, including today. Please pray that everything goes smoothly for all of us," he said.
Another Facebook user, Musfyrah Mansor, was similarly stranded after her morning flight was cancelled.
She said the airline informed passengers that flights would be rescheduled once operations returned to normal.
00fe5bf02d99f97f: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 6 — The Youth and Sports Ministry (KBS) has submitted an initial framework of its Budget 2027 proposals to the Finance Ministry (MOF) for consideration, with grassroots sports development, youth participation and athletes’ welfare among the ministry’s priorities.
Youth and Sports Minister Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari said the framework was prepared based on input gathered through the Madani Youth Budget Tour being conducted in six zones nationwide.
“Although all the tour sessions have not been completed, KBS has obtained various views from youth organisations, sports associations as well as unorganised youths for review and assessment.

“So far, we have held initial discussions with Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan and have submitted the initial framework for MOF’s assessment,” he told reporters after attending the Oregeon Tower Run Series flag off at The TOP Atrium, here today.

The ministry wants to provide more space and opportunities for the public to participate in sports activities, particularly at the grassroots level to produce more reserve athletes and will focus on athletes’ welfare, including those who have retired or had previously contributed to the country, he added.

Dr Mohammed Taufiq said his ministry also takes into account the views of sports associations and youth organisations as well as the needs of youths in rural areas and those who have not previously participated in any ministry organisations or programmes.

He also shared that his ministry intends to hold various nationwide tour programmes in 2027 to reach as many youths as possible, including through large-scale activities and smaller programmes at the community level.

“We want to implement programmes touring throughout Malaysia next year to meet as many young people as possible by carrying out mass activities as well as small-scale activities so that we can engage with every young person,” he said. — Bernama
04b2b79b41e084cf: KUALA LUMPUR: The government must urgently address the chronic shortage of doctors, medical officers (MOs) and specialists in government hospitals, the People's Progressive Party (PPP) said.

Its president, Datuk Dr Loga Bala Mohan, said manpower shortages and the uneven distribution of healthcare personnel were contributing to excessive workloads, longer waiting times, burnout and delays in specialist treatment, with Sabah and Sarawak facing particularly serious challenges.
"This has been a pressing issue for many years, yet a permanent and comprehensive solution remains necessary.

"Delays in addressing the problem will not only affect patients but will also place an unsustainable burden on doctors, MOs, nurses and other healthcare personnel," he told reporters after chairing the party's Supreme Council meeting at its headquarters today.

He said the government must accelerate the abolition of the contract system, provide sufficient permanent positions, fill vacant posts, increase specialist training capacity and address the uneven distribution of doctors.
"We also called for the publication of updated manpower data on approved posts, filled positions and vacancies for doctors, MOs, specialists, nurses and other critical healthcare personnel."
He said PPP continued to receive complaints and appeals from members of the public experiencing delays in obtaining treatment at government healthcare facilities.
"While every case must be assessed individually, the wider manpower shortage is clearly one of the factors contributing to excessive waiting times and pressure on the system."
Citing a report from July last year, Loga Bala said doctors at understaffed facilities were seeing 80 to 100 patients a day, while some patients waited up to 6 hours.
More recently, he said a cancer treatment centre reportedly required 45 to 50 MOs but had only about half that number. On some days, 4 MOs were seeing up to 90 patients at its day-care facility.
"This is extremely worrying, particularly when Malaysia is facing a growing cancer burden and patients require timely diagnosis, treatment and follow-up care.
"The time for another temporary solution has passed. Malaysia needs a permanent, properly funded and sustainable solution to its healthcare manpower crisis," he said.

Fadhlina, who is Nibong Tebal MP, said the government would ensure that all schools received attention in terms of development, maintenance and programmes aimed at strengthening teachers and pupils.
On Friday, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said the Indian community would never be marginalised under the Madani government’s development agenda.
Anwar said this had been addressed through engagements with Indian community leaders to review the progress of the government’s agenda and hear their views and concerns.
He also said various efforts had been mobilised in education, entrepreneurship, microfinancing, welfare and cash assistance to ease the burden on families and improve living standards.

600f88f048cab026: JAKARTA, Sept 6 — Malaysians stranded in Jakarta after volcanic ash from the eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau disrupted flights are now scrambling for alternative arrangements, with some travellers facing delays of several days before they can return home.

One traveller who goes by the moniker Spritzerphilips on Threads was a picture of fatigue and anxiety after being stranded at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport after her flight, scheduled for today, was cancelled.
“Stranded in Indonesia, can’t get back to Malaysia, asked for help from the embassy here but they said they couldn’t help either,” she wrote.
About an hour later, Spritzerphilips said she managed to secure a new flight for Tuesday.
“Hotel is sorted, ticket has also been rescheduled to Tuesday,” she wrote,, adding that she would consider travelling by land to Yogyakarta if the new flight was cancelled.
Other Threads users suggested travelling overland to Yogyakarta or Surabaya to catch a flight to Kuala Lumpur.
Another Malaysian traveller, Muhamad Norshahrizal Norizan, said on Facebook that he and his family had been stranded in Jakarta for two days after their flights were repeatedly cancelled.
“My family and I are stranded, our flight has been cancelled for two days already... today is the same,” he posted.
Facebooker Musfyrah Mansor also said she was stranded at the same airport after her flight was cancelled this morning.
She said her airline had informed passengers that flights would be rescheduled once conditions had returned to normal.
The disruption follows the eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau, which sent volcanic ash into the airspace around Jakarta and forced Soekarno-Hatta International Airport to suspend operations today.
The airport closure disrupted 209 flights and affected 22,798 passengers, according to Indonesia’s Civil Aviation Director General Lukman F Laisa.
Malaysia Airlines and Batik Air have cancelled a combined 20 Malaysia-Jakarta flights today, while AirAsia has cancelled or rescheduled a number of services.
The situation remains fluid as Indonesian authorities monitor the spread of volcanic ash and its impact on flight operations.
b549d3dd1a1f85fb: JAKARTA, Sept 6 — Indonesia’s Anak Krakatoa volcano remains highly active and could intensify despite a significant decline in the strength of volcanic seismic signals recorded today.

Volcanology and Geological Hazard Mitigation Centre (PVMBG) Head Siti Sumilah Rita Susilawati said the volcano’s seismic amplitude had declined significantly, but its dynamics remained very high, with the Geological Agency continuing round-the-clock monitoring.

“The dynamics remain very high, so this decline does not necessarily indicate that the activity has stopped. There is still a possibility that the activity could increase,” she told an online press conference today.

The National Disaster Management Agency (BNPB), in an update today, said the continuous eruption began at about 11.07pm on September 4, accompanied by rumbling and banging sounds as well as lava fountains, while the Geological Agency, in a September 5 special report, said the latest activity was part of a series of eruptions that began on July 2.

On the latest ash distribution as of 10.30am, Siti Sumilah said a dense ash cloud at about 50,000 feet, or 15 kilometres above sea level, had moved away from the active crater and was drifting southwest towards the Indian Ocean.

“At around 20,000 feet, or six kilometres, volcanic ash emissions continuing from the crater vent are being carried westward by the wind, while residual fine ash from the previous eruption phase is shifting eastward towards waters south of the Sunda Strait,” she said.

Meanwhile, Geological Agency Head Lana Saria said Anak Krakatoa remained at Level III (Alert), the second-highest level in Indonesia’s four-tier volcano alert system, with the threats identified in the agency’s overall assessment remained concentrated around the volcano and within the recommended three-kilometre radius.
She said no potential threat to residential areas identified at present.

“The recommended radius may be expanded if there is a significant increase in the energy or scale of the eruptions, volcanic material reaches greater distances, deformation or pressure within the volcano increases, or pyroclastic flows or other hazards emerge beyond the three-kilometre radius,” she said.

According to a 2006 paper by a PVMBG volcanologist published in the Indonesian Journal on Geoscience, Anak Krakatoa emerged above sea level in 1929 within the caldera formed by the catastrophic 1883 Krakatoa eruption, which generated tsunamis that killed more than 36,000 people.

Anak Krakatoa was itself associated with a deadly tsunami nearly 90 years later, with BNPB saying in a 2018 disaster report that an underwater landslide linked to its eruption triggered a tsunami in the Sunda Strait on December 22 that year, killing 437 people. — Bernama
f864e768fa39de50: KUALA LUMPUR: The FA of Malaysia (FAM) could find itself facing the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) over the status of its Electoral Committee chairman.
That is the scenario painted by sports analyst Datuk Dr Pekan Ramli as FAM holds its elections at an Extraordinary Congress on Sept 17.
Pekan warned that proceeding with the election under a "legally vulnerable" Electoral Committee could expose FAM to legal disputes and plunge Malaysian football into further turmoil.

However, he stressed that the fault does not lie with Electoral Committee chairman Professor Datuk Dr Abdullah Mohamad Said, but squarely on FAM and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) for failing to ensure strict adherence to their own updated statutes.
"We do not question Abdullah's integrity, credibility, or his past contributions. He has handled previous elections seamlessly, and his competence is not in doubt," Pekan told Timesport.
"If there has been an oversight, the blame should not fall on Abdullah. The accountability lies with FAM and AFC.

"Once the new electoral code was endorsed, the authorities should have ensured full technical compliance, whether by tabling a fresh motion or appointing someone who meets the specific requirements," he said.
Pekan warned that while the FAM election process may appear smooth going, any aggrieved candidate or affiliate could subsequently challenge the legitimacy of the entire congress.

"If the congress concludes and everyone is satisfied, there may be no issue. But the real danger arises if someone is unhappy with the outcome or disputes why certain candidates were cleared or disqualified.

"Any dissatisfied party can mount a legal challenge on technical grounds. If this dispute is dragged all the way to CAS, the entire election could be nullified. That would cause absolute chaos," he said.

Football observers have warned that beyond a costly showdown at CAS, any statutory discrepancy during the Sept 17 election could invite direct intervention from FIFA. Under Article 8 of the FIFA Statutes, the world governing body holds the power to withhold recognition of election results or, in a worst-case scenario, install an interim Normalisation Committee to take administrative control of FAM and conduct fresh polls.

On Saturday, Timesport reported that FAM could find itself on a legal minefield ahead of its Extraordinary Congress on Sept 17, following mounting questions over whether Abdullah satisfies the mandatory legal qualification explicitly stipulated under the national body's newly adopted electoral rules.
Under the FAM electoral code, endorsed at its congress on June 4, the rules dictate: "The Chairperson and Deputy Chairperson of the Electoral Committee shall be qualified to practise law."

However, public records and academic credentials show that Abdullah, a former deputy vice-chancellor of Universiti Teknologi MARA, holds doctorate and master's degrees in Town and Regional Planning and Environmental Studies, with no documented qualifications as a practising advocate and solicitor.
Abdullah has overseen FAM elections since 2020 and had his mandate extended last year. He recently signed off on the official nomination acceptance letters for the Sept 17 election.

Commercial and sports lawyer Nik Erman Nik Roseli previously told Timesport that the 2026 Code fundamentally altered the baseline prerequisites, requiring the Electoral Committee chairman to be qualified to practise law rather than merely holding a law degree or possessing general legal understanding.
Both FAM and the AFC have declined to comment on the matter.
06770c891f787564: MACHANG, Sept 6 — Water supply to about 34,000 consumer accounts in Machang, southern Kota Bharu and parts of Pasir Puteh is expected to be restored in stages from noon tomorrow following a main pipe leak in Pulai Chondong here.

Kelantan Public Works, Infrastructure, Water and Rural Development Committee chairman Datuk Dr Izani Husin said the leak in the 1,100-millimetre glass-fibre reinforced plastic (GRP) pipe was detected on Friday, with excavation and repair works beginning on the same day.

He said the pipe, which was commissioned in 2018, had a leak measuring about 10 centimetres, while cracks affecting almost half of the pipe were also detected and believed to have been caused by erosion.

“Air Kelantan Sdn Bhd (AKSB) instructed specialist contractors from Kemaman, Terengganu to carry out urgent repairs, which were initially expected to take 10 days but were completed within four days,” he told reporters after inspecting the repair works here today.

Following the disruption, he said 24 lorries and water tankers have been deployed to supply about 1.04 million litres of water a day to affected consumers, including hospitals, dialysis centres, prisons, schools, hostels, educational institutions and residential areas, with assistance from water operators in Kedah, Pahang, Johor, Penang, Selangor and Perak.
Meanwhile, AKSB head of Production Dr Mohd Hilmi P. Ramli said the company planned to replace the GRP pipe with mild steel pipes following the fourth leak since it was commissioned eight years ago.
He said that, in the initial phase, about 800 metres of the 10-kilometre pipeline would be replaced with funding from Pengurusan Aset Air Berhad, at an estimated cost of RM3 million. — Bernama
c1cb435f575bec68: The Reform UK leader is under pressure after senior aides appeared to plot how to bypass electoral laws on foreign donations Farage claims that he faces a disproportionate level of scrutiny compared to the other parties as part of an establishment stitch up, despite having legitimate questions to answer about his party’s finances. Laura Kuenssbergg gave the Reform leader a series of examples of other investigations faced by other party leaders, Farage responded: I don’t think the others have been de-banked. I don’t think the others have been kicked out by their pension provider. I don’t think the others have literally had an attempt to wipe them out of society, oh and their families as well. There is no doubt there is huge political prejudice against Reform right across the corporate world and right across the establishment. And that is a simple fact of life – and why? Because we are the disrupters and that’s the way it works. Continue reading...
f985a74969d6dd88: KATHMANDU: Nepali rescuers faced challenging conditions on Sunday as search operations after catastrophic floods entered their 12th day, buoyed by the extraordinary rescues of four survivors.
The glacial and mountain collapse on the China-Nepal border has killed at least 1,372 people and left more than 5,500 missing across the two countries.
Rescuers found two more people alive yesterday, joining two saved the day before in what have been described as miraculous tales of survival.
Three of those have been found in hydropower tunnels where the government initially said it believed more than 100 workers could be alive.
"Search and rescue is going on at the tunnels despite geography, adverse weather and lack of connectivity," energy minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha told AFP.
"Rescue workers were experiencing multiple challenges," he said.
The wall of icy water and debris tore through mountain districts on Aug 26, destroying roads, bridges and other infrastructure.
On Saturday, rescuers pulled a Chinese man alive from deep inside a hydropower tunnel, and a 64-year-old Nepali woman, Chandrika Shrestha, from her mud-covered home.
Prime minister Balendra Shah said the latter rescue had "given hope to the entire nation".
A day earlier, two Nepali hydropower workers were rescued at the Trishuli 3A tunnel, where searches continue alongside multiple other sites, with at least 12 hydropower projects affected.
Biraj Bhakta Shrestha said work was continuing to restore electricity in several areas.
"Places that have unreachable, we've tried to restore power with solar," he told AFP.
Foreign minister Shisir Khanal has called the disaster a "Himalayan tsunami" and has warned reconstruction costs could run into the billions of dollars.
The UN has said the magnitude of the destruction makes delivering aid an immense challenge, and has launched a US$50 million appeal to help more than 84,000 people.
With mortuaries overflowing, Nepal has buried hundreds of bodies in mass graves, after taking DNA samples for future identification, according to the police.
Only around 100 bodies have been identified and handed over to families.
Nepal will hold a national day of mourning on Monday, the 13th day since the disaster, in line with a traditional period of mourning in Hindu rituals.
While the exact cause of the glacial collapse is unclear, climate change is accelerating glacial melting worldwide, increasing the risk of such disasters.
In Nepal, rescuers have retrieved 1,341 bodies, while around 4,996 people remain missing, according to the disaster agency.
Chinese state media report that 31 people have been killed and 531 are missing in Tibet.
The combined toll is 1,372 dead and more than 5,500 missing, including around 800 foreigners, among them tourists and pilgrims.
615993baca7e3fba: SINGAPORE, Sept 6 — Singapore’s prime minister, Lawrence Wong, has warned that racist and anti-foreigner abuse online cannot be dismissed as harmless chatter, saying prejudice risks becoming normalised and driving communities apart if left unchecked.

In a Facebook post today, Wong said there would always be people seeking to exploit Singapore’s racial and religious differences, but that Singaporeans could choose not to give such views “more space or legitimacy”.
“These views do not represent Singapore. But neither can we dismiss them as harmless online chatter,” he wrote.
“If such behaviour goes unchecked, it can become normalised, deepen mistrust between communities, and pull us apart.”

His comments came after anti-Indian remarks appeared online in the wake of devastating floods in Nepal, where nine Singaporeans remain missing, as well as during discussions over Singapore Airlines’ investment in Air India.
Wong said Singapore should continue to allow robust debate, but warned against using legitimate arguments as cover for prejudice against particular communities or hostility towards foreigners.
“We should be clear about the distinction,” he said.
While it would not be possible to stop every hateful comment online, Wong said Singaporeans could reject such views and refuse to amplify them.
He said Singapore had remained cohesive because it had repeatedly resisted attempts to divide people along racial or religious lines and instead chosen to see one another as fellow Singaporeans.
“We must keep making that choice,” he said, invoking the National Pledge and its commitment to unity “regardless of race, language or religion”.
Wong said he had discussed the issue with Cabinet colleagues, after Senior Minister K. Shanmugam said on Saturday that police were looking into racist and xenophobic comments made online.
Shanmugam described some of the remarks as “shameful, nasty and totally unacceptable”, including comments invoking racist stereotypes about snakes, curry, prata and black magic.
He also said Singapore’s Ministry of Digital Development and Information would ask social media platforms to remove comments that breached their guidelines.
Senior Minister Lee Hsien Loong separately condemned the remarks today, calling them deeply troubling and urging Singaporeans to “reject hatred”.

Wong said such tensions were not new, pointing to anti-foreigner and racial sentiment during the Covid-19 pandemic, debates over the Singapore-India Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement, and the 2025 general election, when he had also warned against bringing race and religion into politics.
Singapore’s national identity, he said, must remain open and inclusive.

“Whatever our background, if we embrace our values and way of life, we are part of this nation. This is what our National Pledge stands for, and I believe the vast majority of Singaporeans share this view,” he wrote.
“We must never allow prejudice against any community to become accepted or normal in Singapore.”
5231e4a1b8d042f2: PETALING JAYA: Seseorang masuk syurga adalah kerana izin dan rahmat Allah, bukan kerana mengundi mana-mana parti politik, kata Timbalan Presiden Amanah, Mujahid Yusof Rawa.

Bekas menteri di Jabatan Perdana Menteri (hal ehwal agama) itu berkata dakwaan bahawa seseorang boleh masuk syurga kerana mengundi parti politik adalah tidak berasas, "dari sudut ilmu mahupun realiti".
"Saya menganggapnya sebagai 'menjual syurga untuk politik' dan pihak berotoriti perlu ambil tindakan sesuai kerana 'menghina agama'," katanya di Facebook.
Mujahid menyoal apakah parti politik yang mentakfirkan sesama Islam dan melabel orang yang tidak bersamanya sebagai munafik akan mengundang rahmat Allah atau bala.
Beliau juga menyoal bagaimana sikap parti yang memfitnah dan berbohong demi kuasa dapat mengundang rahmat Allah untuk dapat syurga.

Kenyataan ini menyusuli laporan yang memetik Setiausaha Agung PAS Takiyuddin Hassan sebagai berkata ungkapan 'masuk PAS akan masuk syurga' mungkin menjadi sindiran terhadap partinya, wajah pwerjuangan mereka berteraskan Islam dan selaras ajaran agama.
Katanya, kalau seseorang mati kerana berjuang mempertahankan Islam, dianggap mati syahid dan diberikan ganjaran pahala, orang itu akan masuk syurga.
Jadi, katanya lagi, jika masuk PAS dan terima Islam, berjuang di atas landasan Islam, dan nakkan Islam di dunia dan akhirnya, orang itu boleh masuk syurga.
Takiyuddin juga berkata keahlian PAS kini melebihi sejuta orang di seluruh negara.
Malaysiakini melaporkan Takiyuddin berkata demikian pada ceramah perdana sempena muktamar ke-75, semalam.
Sementara itu, Timbalan Pengerusi Majlis Ulama Umno, Khairuddin Aman Razali, mempertahankan ucapan Takiyuddin, kerana ia menegaskan kaedah untuk dapat pahala dan dapat syurga dalam berpolitik.
"Bukan semata-mata masuk parti yang membawa ke syurga tetapi cita-cita perjuangan parti yang selaras dengan Islam yang boleh membawa ke syurga," katanya di Facebook.
Katanya, kaedah itu terpakai pada mana-mana parti orang Islam yang lain yang memperjuangkan perkara yang sama iaitu Islam.
Bekas pemimpin PAS itu menambah jika ada tindak-tanduk parti atau individu dan pimpinan parti yang tidak selari dengan Islam, maka nilaian pahala dan dosa dibuat atas setiap perlakuan yang silap itu.
Beliau berkata perlakuan yang silap mesti ditegur dan dibetulkan dari semasa ke semasa kerana tiada seorang pun sunyi daripada kesilapan.
331df2923cdc75a9: TOKYO: The Japanese government recently released guidelines on how to check the specifications of bear repellent sprays and properly choose and use them amid a proliferation of ineffective products on the market, Kyodo News reported.

With public interest in bear sprays growing as the country faces an increase in bear sightings and attacks, the Environment Ministry and the Consumer Affairs Agency have urged manufacturers and distributors to provide information on the efficacy of their products.
Unlike the United States, Japan has no uniform standards for such sprays.
According to the ministry and other sources, the main component in a repellent is capsaicin, the active chemical compound in chilli peppers.

The concentration of the ingredient in the product should be around 1 to 2 per cent, while the spray should have a range of at least 7.5 metres and a continuous spray duration of at least six seconds, according to the ministry's guidance.
"Some products rebranded for bears were actually made for use against people," said Shinjiro Sasaki, a ministry official who also recommended that people practice using the repellents.
The recently released warnings also urged people not to carry bear sprays unless necessary, to purchase products with a safety latch and to store them out of reach of children.
There were more than 50,000 bear encounters in the year ended March, a record high and double the year-earlier level, according to government data.
"Using the repellent sprays should be a last resort," Environment Minister Hirotaka Ishihara said at a press conference.
"We ask people to also take other countermeasures such as moving in large groups."
c3a7f701a5a2be40: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — The term ‘religious exploitation’ is more appropriate and objective than ‘riding on religion’ to describe the act of misusing religion for worldly interests, said Federal Territories Mufti Ahmad Fauwaz Fadzil.

He said the term ‘riding on religion’ should not be used indiscriminately as it could lead to generalisations about religious figures, including scholars and preachers who sincerely champion the cause of Islam.

The term ‘religious exploitation’ focuses more specifically on the act of misusing religion to gain wealth, influence or position, while also more clearly illustrating the existence of those who take advantage and those who are deceived.
“On the other hand, the term ‘riding’ has a negative and harsh connotation and tends to carry elements of sarcasm and personal accusations against the perpetrator.

“The term ‘religious exploitation’ more accurately describes the power structure in this phenomenon, namely the existence of those who take advantage (exploit) and those who are exploited (members of the public who are deceived or misled), in line with the actual meaning of the evidence from the Quran and Sunnah,” he said in the Tinta Mufti column published by the Federal Territories Mufti Department today.

Ahmad Fauwaz said the exploitation of religion was prohibited and condemned in the Quran, including through verses in Surah At-Taubah and Surah Al-Baqarah, both of which illustrate forms of religious exploitation that occur when religion is manipulated as a tool to obtain wealth and worldly interests, an act that is reprehensible as it exploits the name of Allah for personal gain.

He said the Prophet Muhammad also warned against those who use religion to deceive people for worldly interests, as narrated by al-Tirmidhi, which means: “At the end of time, a group of men will emerge who deceive people by using religion to obtain worldly gains... their tongues are sweeter than sweets, while their hearts are the hearts of wolves.”

Ahmad Fauwaz said the hadith described individuals who present themselves as knowledgeable and pious to gain the trust of the community, while using religion as a guise to obtain money, influence or position.

In this regard, he advised the public not to be easily deceived by outward appearances, but instead to conduct proper checks before placing their trust, wealth or obedience in any individual who uses religion as a tool for personal gain.

At the same time, he reminded those involved in preaching, religious knowledge and religious work to always maintain sincerity and fulfil their responsibilities solely for the sake of Allah and to attain His pleasure. — Bernama
5fd621f0097574f9: SERDANG, Sept 6 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security could receive a bigger allocation in Budget 2027, provided the ministry continues to uphold good governance.
His remarks came after its minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu called for an additional allocation during the closing ceremony of the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Exhibition here.

Anwar, who is also finance minister, said additional funding could be considered as long as the ministry ensured that public money was managed properly and reached farmers, fishermen and paddy planters.
“Because large expenditures must be managed well, and we have no choice.
“If we want to safeguard the fate of farmers, paddy planters, and traders, we must ensure good management.
“Allocations may increase, but if there are leakages and misappropriation, those who suffer are the farmers, fishermen, and paddy planters,” he said.
Speaking to reporters later, Mohamad who is better known as Mat Sabu, said the additional allocation is to allow his ministry to prepare early for potential challenges next year.
He said this includes measures to deal with the El Niño phenomenon, which is expected to continue into early next year.
The ministry also needs to be prepared for a possible spike in fertiliser prices amid ongoing geopolitical tensions, he said.
“Our secretary-general has already mapped out our requirements and early measures, particularly if temperatures surge.
“Aquaculture will take a hit. We’re looking at potential fish loss and similar issues. So we must have aid ready to deploy.
“And that’s just one scenario out of many. Say there’s a sudden surge in fertiliser prices; we then need to ask the government for financial support as well,” Mohamad said.
He said the request is essentially for supplementary funds, and that it can be adjusted according to how conditions develop later.
The government will table Budget 2027 when the Dewan Rakyat sits again next month.
2a13100ac7bdd63a: ABOUT 20 Chinese rescue workers in bright orange operated excavators, shovels and ground-penetrating radar detectors on Sunday in an effort to find hundreds of people missing since a tsunami-like mudslide destroyed China's main border crossing with Nepal.
The Gyirong border crossing separating China's Tibet and Nepal became a grisly emblem of the devastation that followed the collapse of a glacier on the Nepal side of the border on Aug 26.
Reuters and other news agencies visited the land port, which sits in a narrow river gorge, in the first trip organised for foreign media by China's foreign ministry.
There was no trace of the five-storey Chinese customs building that had stood at the border before the disaster, video and pictures from the scene showed.
The only structure still visible from before the mudslide was a portion of a nearby water tower installation.
Workers had placed a Chinese flag at the spot where the border gate, at nearly 20-meters-tall, once stood.
Behind hazard signs that read "Danger Area Pass Quickly", three groups of about 20 rescue and recovery workers dug the earth using shovels while several red excavators stood by on Sunday afternoon.
Rescue workers have divided the search area into seven zones, officials told Reuters. They have completed searches in four of them, with three remaining.
The mudslide has killed more than 1,300 people on both sides of the border, with more than 5,000 missing.
On Saturday, emergency crews in Nepal rescued a Chinese worker who had been in a tunnel linked to a hydropower station.
On China's side of the border, 31 people had been confirmed dead while 531 others were still classified as missing as of Friday.
Among those still unaccounted for are 261 foreigners from 23 countries, Chinese officials have said.
Gyirong County sits at an average altitude of more than 4,000 meters, though the port itself lies lower, at around 1,800 meters.
The risk of landslides, poor weather and deep mud has further complicated rescue and recovery efforts.
The only land route into Gyirong was restored by Wednesday morning, allowing China to bring in heavy equipment to aid recovery and eventual rebuilding.
State media has shown workers restoring power to the area by sinking temporary electric poles to reconnect it to the grid.

Gyirong has emerged as the main border crossing for travelers and trade between Nepal and Tibet over the past decade, after a 2015 earthquake in Nepal badly damaged an alternative crossing farther east.
The port was shut down between July last year and January because of an earlier glacial flood.
In addition to a shipment point to Nepal for Chinese goods, including electric cars, it had also become a crossing point for thousands of Hindu pilgrims in recent years.
Many Hindus travel through Nepal to Mount Kailash, a high-altitude site in Tibet revered by Hindus and Buddhists. Hindus believe it to be the eternal home of Lord Shiva and his wife Parvati.
Many of the foreign nationals still missing in Tibet were pilgrims with extended families in India, diplomats in Beijing have said.
There are 49 Indian citizens among the missing.
* The writers are from Reuters

574d85305558d06a: ALOR SETAR, Sept 6 — The Kedah state government appealed for the continuation of cloud seeding operations, coordinated by the National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA), to help raise declining water levels at dams in the state.

State Public Works, Natural Resources, Water Supply, Water Resources and Environment Committee chairman Datuk Mohamad Yusoff Zakaria said that while the operation carried out from Thursday to yesterday resulted in rain, it was still insufficient to boost reservoir levels.
He said before cloud seeding on Sept 2, total water supply at the Pedu, Muda and Ahning Dams stood at 37.14 per cent, but had dropped to 36.64 per cent this morning.
“The water level at Pedu Dam is now at 38.46 per cent, compared to 39.02 per cent on Sept 2, while Muda Dam recorded 9.04 per cent, down from 9.32 per cent previously,” he told Bernama today.
Meanwhile, supply at Ahning Dam stood at 45.00 per cent, compared to 45.32 per cent over the same period.
He said sufficient dam water supply is critical to ensure the smooth operation of padi irrigation systems, as Kedah’s agricultural sector is heavily dependent on these water sources.

Earlier, the federal government took early and targeted measures to address dry weather conditions, low rainfall, and the risk of deteriorating air quality through cloud seeding operations in Kedah and Perlis. — Bernama
bd9fcf9142cb3270: KUALA LUMPUR: M-League players will have to play through "unhealthy" air pollution, with the Malaysian Football League (MFL) setting an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 201 as the threshold for postponing matches.
The decision means Super League and FA Cup matches will go ahead when API readings are between 101 and 200, a range classified as "unhealthy".
Readings between 201 and 300 are deemed "very unhealthy".
The MFL directive is contained in a special Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) circular dated Aug 26 and signed by chief executive officer Shazli Shaik.
It was sent to clubs in both competitions.
In the circular, the MFL said the congested 2026-27 calendar was a key reason for allowing matches to continue.

"MFL recommends that matches proceed due to the congestion of the 2026-2027 Malaysian League schedule and calendar, unless API readings reach very hazardous levels that are detrimental to health," said Shazli.
Under the league's haze SOP, the match commissioner monitors hourly readings from the Department of Environment (DOE), starting three hours before kick-off.
If the API reaches 101, matches will continue, with "cooling breaks" introduced under Article 2.40 of the Malaysia League Rules.
The breaks, usually around the 30th and 75th minutes, last between 90 seconds and three minutes.
Players can use the time to take ice, drink water and cool down before returning to the pitch.
Matches can only be postponed once the API reaches 201.
Even then, officials can wait up to 60 minutes, in two 30-minute periods, to see if air quality improves.
For matches that go ahead, host venues must keep medical rooms open and identify nearby hospitals.
Substitute players and technical staff are also advised to wear face masks and return to their hotels after the match.
The policy comes as haze has already disrupted the domestic calendar.

On Sept 1, the FA Cup round-of-16 match between DPMM and Terengganu at Hassanal Bolkiah National Stadium was called off just hours before kick-off after the Brunei Darussalam Ministry of Health intervened when Bandar Seri Begawan's API reached 215.
The postponement led to further changes, with MFL announcing revisions to the Super League schedule on Sept 2 before several FA Cup matches were rescheduled on Sept 4.
The decision to allow matches to continue when API readings are between 101 and 200 has also raised health concerns.
Under Health Ministry (MOH) guidelines, members of the public are advised to avoid strenuous outdoor activities when the API exceeds 100.
Professional footballers also breathe much more heavily during intense exercise, potentially increasing their exposure to polluted air.
The issue comes as Youth and Sports Minister Dr Taufiq Johari touched on outdoor sporting activities during the haze.
Speaking in Penang today, Taufiq said sporting activities would be stopped when air pollution reached dangerous levels.
"Where the API is very high and in the red zone, like in Serian, Sarawak, we will definitely prohibit any outdoor activities from being held," said Taufiq.

"Every sporting event must adhere to ministry approvals and government guidelines. Our priority is the health of athletes and the overall community. But where the API is low, safe, or moderate, we still permit it."

Earlier, following Cabinet discussions on the transboundary haze, Taufiq said the Youth and Sports Ministry was working with the National Sports Institute (NSI) and National Sports Council (NSC) to ensure national athletes' training schedules were not affected unnecessarily, provided safety guidelines were followed.
However, there is no clear instruction to stop outdoor sports throughout the "unhealthy" API range of 101 to 200, allowing the MFL to use its own threshold of 201 for postponements.
Meanwhile, four sports at the Selangor Para Sukma were postponed after the API reached an unhealthy 169 in Shah Alam and Klang.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd
c94ba8b9a998ec8b: PETALING JAYA: Police have launched an investigation after a two-year-old girl was allegedly attacked by stray dogs near her grandmother's house in Sungai Kelambu, Johor, yesterday morning.
Batu Pahat police chief Shahrulannuar Mushaddat Abdullah Sani confirmed receiving a report over the incident and said the case is being probed under the Child Act 2001, Berita Harian reported.

The Malay daily reported the child's grandmother, Darlinda Darlis, as saying that the incident happened around 7am after her granddaughter, Nur Haira Watikah Hazimi, and her siblings were dropped off at her house.
She said that she had left Nur Haira with the other children while she took a shower. However, later the two-year-old was missing and Darlinda discovered that the front door was open.
She said she then saw her grandchild being attacked by about five dogs outside the house. The child suffered serious injuries to her head and face.
Darlinda said her son immediately took the child to Sultanah Nora Ismail Hospital, where she was treated in the red zone and had to be placed in an induced coma.
“Not long after that, Nur Haira was transferred to Sultanah Aminah Hospital in Johor Bahru due to the severity of her injuries,” she was quoted as saying.
Darlinda said the stray dogs were believed to have been abandoned by people who hunted wild boar in a nearby oil palm plantation.
d3de6daae41e1d56: PUTRAJAYA: Sebanyak 31 penerbangan ke Jakarta dibatalkan di semua lapangan terbang seluruh negara hari ini susulan penutupan sementara Lapangan Terbang Antarabangsa Soekarno-Hatta berikutan abu vulkanik yang terhasil daripada letusan Gunung Anak Krakatau.
Menurut Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB), pembatalan yang dilaporkan syarikat penerbangan setakat tengah hari ini, melibatkan penerbangan yang dijadualkan antara 6.45 pagi hingga 11.55 malam.

Pengendali lapangan terbang itu menjelaskan Lapangan Terbang Antarabangsa Kuala Lumpur (KLIA) mencatat bilangan pembatalan tertinggi dengan 21 penerbangan meliputi 15 di Terminal 1 dan enam di Terminal 2.

"Lapangan Terbang Antarabangsa Pulau Pinang merekodkan enam pembatalan, manakala Lapangan Terbang Antarabangsa Kuching mencatat satu pembatalan, Lapangan Terbang Subang dua dan Lapangan Terbang Kota Bharu dengan satu pembatalan," katanya kepada Bernama hari ini.

Gunung Anak Krakatau, yang terletak di Selat Sunda antara Jawa dan Sumatera, terus meletus sehingga Sabtu, dengan pihak berkuasa melaporkan aktiviti pancutan lava dan bunyi dentuman dan gemuruh yang boleh didengar dari sebuah pos pemerhatian.
Letusan itu bermula pada 11.07 malam waktu tempatan pada Jumaat dan berterusan sepanjang pemerhatian dari tengah malam hingga 6 pagi semalam.

Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi Indonesia melaporkan adh gunung berapi dikenal pasti setinggi 6,000 meter di bahagian Jawa gunung berapa itu manakala kepulan sehingga 15,000 meter di bahagian Sumatera dan beberapa bahagian wilayah Banten di Jawa.
Operasi penerbangan di Lapangan Terbang Antarabangsa Soekarno-Hatta telah digantung sehingga 1.30 tengah hari, waktu tempatan hari ini (2.30 petang, waktu Malaysia).

Terdahulu, akaun media sosial rasmi KLIA mengeluarkan nasihat perjalanan yang menggesa penumpang menuju ke Jakarta menerusi penerbangan yang terjejas supaya menghubungi syarikat penerbangan masing-masing untuk maklumat jadual terkini.
KLIA memaklumkan kawasan rehat telah disediakan untuk penumpang yang terjejas menunggu berita selanjutnya.
281c35722231ca73: KUALA LUMPUR: Police are closely monitoring major highways nationwide as motorists begin making their way home following the school holidays.

Bukit Aman Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department (TEID) director Datuk Seri Mohammed Hasbullah Ali said highway patrol units were on the ground monitoring traffic conditions and ensuring the safety of road users.
He said police expected an increase in the number of vehicles on major highways as families returned home ahead of the resumption of school and work.
"Our highway patrol units are on the ground and we are monitoring the situation, particularly along the major highways.
"We urge motorists to plan their journeys properly, remain patient and, most importantly, obey traffic regulations throughout their journey," he told the New Straits Times today.
Hasbullah reminded motorists not to rush despite potentially heavier traffic and longer travelling times.
He said drivers should ensure they were sufficiently rested before embarking on long-distance journeys and stop at a safe location to rest if they began feeling tired or sleepy.
"Do not force yourself to continue driving when you are tired. Fatigue can affect your concentration and reaction time.
"Motorists should also avoid speeding, tailgating or making dangerous lane changes simply to save a few minutes on their journey," he said.
Hasbullah also reminded motorists not to use mobile phones while driving, stressing that their attention should remain on the road at all times.
He advised motorists to check their vehicles before travelling, particularly the tyres, brakes, lights and other essential components, to reduce the risk of breakdowns or accidents.
Motorists, he added, should wear their seat belts, while motorcyclists and pillion riders must use properly fastened helmets.
He also urged road users to exercise patience in congested areas and refrain from misusing the emergency lane.
"Give way to ambulances, police, fire and rescue vehicles and other emergency vehicles when necessary," he said.
Hasbullah said motorists should also maintain a safe following distance, use their indicators before changing lanes and observe speed limits.
He urged road users to take extra precautions during bad weather, including reducing their speed and increasing the distance between their vehicles and the one ahead.
"Everyone wants to reach home safely. There is no need to rush or take unnecessary risks.
"Be courteous to other road users, follow the rules and make safety your priority throughout the journey," he said.
c0354da0abdd1248: BEIRUT, Sept 6 — Lebanon said four people were killed today in strikes which Israel said it carried out after Hezbollah had launched drones at its soldiers in south Lebanon, the latest escalation amid a fragile truce.
Lebanon’s health ministry reported two people killed in south Lebanon’s Nabatieh al-Fawqa and two women killed in nearby Arab Salim.

It said 20 other people including several women and three children were wounded in those locations as well as in the city of Nabatieh and the town of Kfar Rumman, adding that the toll was provisional.
Israel’s army said it was striking south Lebanon after Hezbollah fighters launched two drones towards Israeli soldiers operating in Israel’s self-declared “security zone” in the south.
It slammed a “blatant violation” by Hezbollah, without reporting troop casualties in the incident.

Shortly before the statement, Israel’s military had issued its first evacuation notice in Lebanon in several weeks, warning residents near a building it identified as a Hezbollah “facility” in Arab Salim to evacuate ahead of an attack on the site.
It did not issue warnings for other areas where strikes were reported.
Lebanon’s state-run National News Agency (NNA) said that after the Israeli warning for the building, “enemy warplanes launched a strike on another house, destroying it” and killing the two women.
It said the Israeli military subsequently “carried out a strike on the home” threatened in the evacuation warning.
‘Security zone’
The NNA said a strike in Nabatieh al-Fawqa destroyed part of the Ghandour hospital, adding that it had been out of service for years.

It also said a heavy airstrike on Nabatieh city targeted a historical building and damaged offices belonging to state finance and agriculture authorities, while shops and cafes in the vicinity were also damaged.
It also reported a strike on a motorcycle in the area.
Lebanon was drawn into the Middle East war in March after Hezbollah attacked Israel in support of its backer Iran.
Israel responded with airstrikes and a ground invasion that Lebanon says have killed more than 4,300 people.
Israeli forces are still operating inside a self-declared “security zone” around 10 kilometres (six miles) deep inside Lebanon along the border.
Violence has lessened since a US-Iran memorandum of understanding on the broader conflict in June, while Israel and Lebanon signed a framework agreement later that month.
But Lebanon still reports Israeli strikes, artillery shelling and broad demolitions of civilian buildings in southern villages and towns.

On Friday, Israeli strikes in the country’s south and east killed four people including an 18-year-old woman, authorities said, as Israel said it struck Hezbollah targets in response to a drone launch towards its soldiers.
Earlier this week, Israel said it had taken “operational control” of the strategic Ali al-Taher ridge near Nabatieh.
Hezbollah has not commented on the announcement or confirmed that Israel has captured the site.
Also this week, the International Committee of the Red Cross facilitated the transfer to Lebanon of five people detained by Israel.
Israel and Lebanon began direct negotiations after the latest hostilities erupted, with fresh talks expected this month, though no date has been announced. — AFP
3313ceed4f70a951: TOKYO, Sept 6 — The Japan Meteorological Agency warned of heavy downpours in Tokyo and six other prefectures through Monday, citing the combined effects of a typhoon and a seasonal rain front, reported Xinhua.

People in the Japanese capital and six other prefectures — Saitama, Kanagawa, Chiba, Shizuoka, Aichi and Mie — were advised to stay alert as a linear rainband was forecast to develop, unleashing torrential rain within a span of just a few hours.
The weather agency also cautioned that landslides, flooding in low-lying areas and swollen rivers were possible risks across parts of eastern Japan.

A seasonal front has lingered south of the Japanese archipelago, and atmospheric conditions have grown unstable as warm, moist air from Typhoon Krovanh feeds into it. The front is expected to move northward heading into Monday, the agency said. — Bernama-Xinhua
3b7c952e7cbf7d23: TEHRAN: Iranian authorities have arrested a number of people accused of appearing in a rare video waving the flag of an outlawed opposition group, state television said Sunday.

Videos circulating online in recent days showed individuals riding motorbikes on empty streets in Iran while waving the white-and-red banner of the banned People's Mujahedin Organisation of Iran (MEK).
On Sunday, state television said authorities had identified and arrested "all the individuals who appeared in this clip" and that they were "associated" with MEK, without specifying how many.
It said the motorcade had been travelling near the city of Karaj, west of Tehran, but it was not clear when the footage was recorded.

Founded in the 1960s in opposition to Iran's then Western-backed shah, the MEK was outlawed after the 1979 Islamic revolution and later fought alongside Saddam Hussein's forces during the Iran-Iraq war.
The group has for decades advocated regime change in Iran from abroad, while Tehran has accused its members of cooperating with its arch-enemy, Israel.
Iran has been at war with the US since Feb 28, when US-Israeli strikes killed the Islamic republic's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei along with senior military officials.
Iran retaliated with attacks across the region as the conflict spread.
e5c6e784383eca5f: KUALA LUMPUR: The Komuniti Madani initiative should play a greater role as a bridge between the government and the people, Bandar Tun Razak member of Parliament Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail said.

She said this role was crucial to ensure that every government policy and initiative reached its intended targets, while also effectively channelling public feedback to the relevant agencies for further action.

"Do not merely be information transmitters; be attentive listeners to the issues affecting the elderly, families in distress and the needs of the youth," she said at the Komuniti Madani appointment certificate ceremony for the Bandar Tun Razak parliamentary constituency here today.

Also present were the Prime Minister's political secretary Datuk Azman Abidin, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya Federal Territories Information Department director Normaizatulakmal Tujad, and Bandar Tun Razak Komuniti Madani chairman Jonathan Vela.
The Prime Minister's wife said that as the government's eyes and ears, community members must be proactive in following up on issues faced by the public.
She said while Komuniti Madani might not be able to resolve every issue raised, the network must ensure that each concern reached those with the authority and responsibility to act.
Meanwhile, she said the initiative must also serve as a frontline defence against the spread of false information, particularly in the age of social media.
"Misinformation spreads rapidly and can disrupt harmony. Komuniti Madani must be the first line of defence against falsehoods, adhering to the principle: 'Check before sharing'.
"We may have differing views, but we must always maintain mutual respect," she said.
Dr Wan Azizah said the true strength of any community lay in the relationships between neighbours and the willingness of people of diverse races and backgrounds to help and support one another.
In this regard, Dr Wan Azizah said the appointees must uphold trust and integrity, proactively engage with the community and listen closely to the people's concerns.

At the ceremony, Dr Wan Azizah also presented the Komuniti Madani Ambassador Award to Azizi Anas and S. Yugan, as well as appointment certificates to representatives from six sub-zones within Bandar Tun Razak.
Komuniti Madani is a rebranding of the 1,878 Komuniti Keluarga Malaysia groups following the launch of the Malaysia Madani framework on Jan 19, 2023.

In the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, 72 Komuniti Madani groups have been established, with the network's strength depending on volunteers who dedicate their time and energy to serving the community.
22722cdf6b934a1b: PETALING JAYA: Kanak-kanak berusia dua tahun parah diserang lima anjing liar dalam kejadian di hadapan rumahnya neneknya, di Kampung Tambak, Peserai, Batu Pahat.
Dalam kejadian sekitar 7 pagi semalam, Nur Haira Watikah Mohammad Hamizi, ditemui nenek, Darlinda Darlis, 56, dalam keadaan terbaring dengan kepala dipenuhi darah.
"Saya menjerit lihat cucu terbaring dengan kepala dan mula dipenuhi darah, dikelilingi lima ekor anjing," katanya kepada Berita Harian.

Katanya, Nur Haira yang parah di kepala dan muka dibawa ke Hospital Sultanah Nora Ismail (HSNI) sebelum dirawat di zon merah dan terpaksa ditidurkan. Kanak-kanak itu kemudian dipindahkan Hospital Sultanah Aminah (HSA) Johor Bahru.

"Saya tak boleh bayangkan keadaannya ketika itu, saya nampak mata dia terbuka namun tidak bercakap. Saya hanya menangis sepanjang perjalanan ke hospital kerana tidak sanggup melihat keadaannya," katanya.
Darlinda berkata, anjing liar yang menyerang cucunya disyaki ditinggalkan individu yang memburu babi di kebun sawit dekat rumahnya.
"Mereka (pemburu) menggunakan anjing dan selepas selesai memburu, mereka tinggalkan anjing di sini. Kami sudah lama risau dengan anjing liar ini yang cepat membiak," katanya.
Sementara itu, Ketua Polis Batu Pahat Shahrulanuar Mushaddat Abdullah Sani, mengesahkan laporan dan siasatan dijalankan mengikut Akta Kanak-kanak 2001.
008750bd1b6fa6dd: KANGAR, Sept 6 — The remand of a 55-year-old activist detained over social media posts linked to a gathering concerning the demolition of a Hindu temple in Bukit Lagi has been extended by two days as police pursue a separate criminal trespass investigation.
Magistrate Ana Rozana Mohd Nor allowed the police application today for the extension, with the activist being investigated under Section 447 of the Penal Code, Harian Metro reported today.

Kangar district police chief Assistant Commissioner Yusharifuddin Mohd Yusop confirmed with the Malay newspaper that the suspect would remain in custody until tomorrow to assist investigations into the alleged criminal trespass.

The activist was initially remanded for two days from September 5 to assist investigations into allegedly inciting social media posts related to the organisation of a gathering over the demolition of the Sri Veera Maha Kaliamman Kovil temple in Bukit Lagi.
He was arrested in Petaling Jaya, Selangor last Thursday following 15 police reports lodged between August 22 and 27 over posts made through his TikTok account.
The earlier investigation is being conducted under Section 4(1) of the Sedition Act 1948 and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
Police had said the posts included a picture promoting the Perhimpunan Merah Maha Kali gathering, which was held at the temple site on August 30.
The temple was demolished by the authorities on August 20, with police previously saying the gathering was believed to have been organised in response to dissatisfaction over the demolition.
Police had also warned that the gathering could potentially trigger racial and religious tensions in Perlis.
afcab96371eb075c: JAKARTA, Sept 6 — Indonesia has designated three airports across Java as alternatives for domestic and international flights diverted due to volcanic ash from Anak Krakatoa.
This comes as the number of airport closures rose to six after Husein Sastranegara Airport in Bandung, West Java, was shut at noon on Sunday.

Transportation Minister Dudy Purwagandhi said the alternatives include Kertajati International Airport in Majalengka, West Java, Jenderal Ahmad Yani International Airport in Semarang, Central Java, and Juanda International Airport in Sidoarjo, East Java.
“There are several airports in Java that we are preparing as alternatives for landings by flights from outside Java as well as international flights,” he told an online press conference on Sunday.

The five other airports affected are Soekarno-Hatta International Airport, Radin Inten II Airport in Lampung, Halim Perdanakusuma Airport, Pondok Cabe Airport and Budiarto Airport, which were closed earlier in the day.
Dudy said all six would remain shut for at least another four hours after the latest tests continued to indicate the presence of volcanic ash.
Amid the continued closures, he said Kertajati was already being used as an alternative, with two Garuda Indonesia flights from Jeddah and Madinah having been diverted there.

“So far, based on the results of tests conducted at Kertajati Airport, it has not yet been affected and operations are still possible,” he said, adding that airlines had been asked to remain vigilant given the dynamic weather conditions and the possibility of volcanic ash spreading towards the airport.

On services for affected passengers, Dudy said airlines had been asked to promptly inform passengers of flight cancellations and facilitate cancellations and ticket refunds electronically so they would not need to travel to the airports.

He said the ministry encouraged the public and businesses to consider rail, road and sea transport, which had so far not been affected by the eruption, including for the movement of goods normally transported by air.

Meanwhile, Dudy said ferry services across the Sunda Strait, where Anak Krakatoa is located between the islands of Java and Sumatra, remained operational, with no additional vessels deployed on the Merak-Bakauheni route as passenger numbers had declined amid the eruption. — Bernama
e7fe383ae0ffef06: KUALA LUMPUR: The People's Progressive Party (PPP) is open to the idea of cooperation between Barisan Nasional (BN) and Pas, but wants to assess its pros and cons before taking a position.
Its president, Datuk Dr Loga Bala Mohan, said the party also needed to determine how such cooperation could benefit BN.

"When you talk about cooperation or understanding, they are 2 different things. So, Umno-Pas cooperation is something to do with race and religion. So, we cannot interfere in race and religion issues.

"However, in terms of having BN, it is a different story. We have to see the pros and cons. So, our stand will be that we are open to the idea to listen and see how it can benefit," he told reporters after chairing the party's Supreme Council meeting at its headquarters today.

Loga Bala was responding to a question on PPP's stand following remarks by former Elected Representatives Council (Mubarak) president Datuk Mohd Rozali Isohak that growing cooperation between Pas and Umno should be sustained at least until the 16th General Election (GE16).
He said any such cooperation would also have to take into account concerns among non-Malays and non-Muslims over Pas' presence.
"Generally, there is a fear. There is nothing else but fear among non-Malays and non-Muslims, who think that Pas' existence will cause a big dent in their lifestyle.
"So, the onus will fall on Pas on how to eradicate that fear and encourage them to come and join the rest of Malaysians.
"I don't think there is an issue with the Malay-Muslim community, but the non-Muslim community in Malaysia will have this problem."
On Sept 5, Rozali, a former Kelantan deputy Menteri Besar, said such cooperation should have taken place long ago.
Rozali said the cooperation could strengthen Malay and Muslim unity after years of waiting for the 2 major Malay-based parties to work together.
b0204e6ac55f721c: KUALA LUMPUR: The race for the FA of Malaysia (FAM) presidency may be a straight fight between two men, but questions over the fairness of the election have shone a light on the relationship between the national body and the Malaysian Football League (MFL).

At the centre of the debate is MFL chairman Datuk Ab Ghani Hassan, who is challenging FA of Selangor (FAS) deputy president Datuk Seri Shahril Mokhtar for the FAM presidential post at the Sept 17 extraordinary congress.

Notably, Ghani is contesting the top FAM post while maintaining his position as MFL president, which gives him an ex-officio route into FAM's executive committee (exco) by virtue of being FAM vice-president 2 under its constitution.
That has led to former FAM head of marketing Sayf Ismail questioning whether the electoral playing field is level, arguing that Ghani faces less risk than the other candidates.
However, the issue is not whether Ghani is violating FAM's statutes.

Asian Football Confederation (AFC) general secretary Datuk Seri Windsor Paul clarified in July that there is no provision requiring an MFL president to relinquish his position to contest the FAM presidency.
"However, should Ghani secure a majority vote for the (FAM) presidential post, he would be required to vacate his MFL position with immediate effect." Windsor reportedly said.

Under the present situation, Ghani would retain his MFL post even if he loses (the contest for the FAM presidency) and, by extension, continue his ex-officio route to the FAM exco as FAM vice-president 2.
Sayf argued that this creates an advantage over the other 22 candidates contesting FAM exco positions, as they will have no other positions if they lose.
"Is the FAM election fair? Unlike all other candidates contesting, Ghani has an unfair advantage.
"He is guaranteed an exco seat even if he loses the presidential race," Sayf said.
"He is already guaranteed the FAM vice-president 2 seat by virtue of his position as MFL president.
"This is unfair to all the 22 other candidates who, if they lose, walk away empty-handed.
"Ghani, on the other hand, is confirmed an exco seat no matter what happens."

Sayf has called on Ghani to either relinquish the MFL president's post before the Sept 17 election and contest on the same terms as the other candidates, or withdraw from the presidential race and keep his MFL position before taking up the vice-president 2 role after the congress.
"To be fair to the other candidates and demonstrate personal integrity in this election, Ghani has two choices.

"Relinquish his position as MFL president prior to Sept 17 and contest on equal footing with the same risks as everyone else, or withdraw from the FAM presidential race and take up the vice-president 2 seat post-Sept 17 under the MFL ticket.
"This is a very serious matter if FAM and Malaysian football want to step forward on the right foot," he said.
The debate comes as FAM faces questions over its governance and administrative structures.
An AFC maturity assessment of FAM has identified shortcomings across 10 of its 11 operational divisions, adding pressure on FAM to strengthen its governance, legal and administrative framework.
The MFL-FAM relationship has attracted attention. FAM is the national governing body responsible for regulatory and representative matters, while MFL oversees the M-League.
Although the MFL was established as a separate entity, its president's ex-officio position within FAM means the two institutions remain directly connected at executive level.
