40dc1ce96b111174: The prospect of a negative leap second – combined with decades of irritation over leap seconds generally – looks set to inspire a bit of global procrastination among international timekeepers. Next month, the General Conference on Weights and Measures is set to vote on effectively calling time on leap seconds. A draft resolution [PDF] would make Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) continuous from May 20, 2027, and allow the difference between UTC and UT1, a measure of time based on Earth's rotation, to reach as much as one hour. Leap seconds keep UTC, which is based on atomic clocks, within 0.9 seconds of time determined by the slightly wobbly rotation of our home planet. Since the system was introduced in 1972, 27 leap seconds have been added to UTC. The urgency comes partly from a slight increase in Earth's rotational speed in recent years, raising the possibility of an adjustment never attempted before: a negative leap second. Experts convened by international timekeeping bodies estimated a 30 percent probability that one would be needed by 2035. Many computer systems were designed on the assumption that a leap second would always be added rather than removed, explained Setnam Shemar, principal scientist at the UK's National Physical Laboratory (NPL). "Most digital architectures and network time servers are hardcoded under the assumption that leap seconds are strictly additive. Losing a second could trigger severe disruption across critical national infrastructure, including telecommunications, electricity grids, and satellite navigation systems," he said. The risks posed by a negative leap second – and leap seconds generally – are behind the proposal to let UTC diverge from rotational time by as much as an hour, which is due to be put to a vote in October. Shemar said the proposal would remove the need for further leap-second adjustments for many years. "This would remove the risks entirely for a very long time. Next month's resolution is likely to pass since it will be based on the outcome of a majority vote of the national delegates from many different countries, and most of them have been keen to end leap seconds for several years due to the risks posed to national infrastructure." UTC would be unlikely to diverge from rotational time by a full hour for at least a thousand years, Shemar said. If humankind lasts that long, it might be the least of our worries. ®
0c9f5588047e946f: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — Professional mixed doubles pair Hoo Pang Ron-Lai Pei Jing’s hopes of landing maiden World Tour title were dashed after they went down 19-21, 16-21 to world No. 1 and home favourites Feng Yan Zhe-Huang Dong Ping in the final of the 2026 China Masters Badminton Championships in Shenzhen today.

During the Super 750 tournament in Shenzhen Arena, Pang Ron-Pei Jing, put up a spirited performance, especially towards the end of the opening game, saving three game points against Yan Zhe-Dong Ping before narrowly losing 19-21.
In the second game, the unseeded Malaysians traded points with the 2026 World Championships runners-up until 5-5 before gradually losing momentum and trailing 8-14.
A wayward smash from Pang Ron handed the Chinese pair the decisive point for a 21-16 victory in 50 minutes for their second China Masters title, following their maiden triumph in the 2024 edition.
Pang Ron-Pei Jing took home US$43,750 (RM176,946) as runners-up while the champions pocketed US$92,500 (RM374,116).
Today’s result marked Pang Ron-Pei Jing’s best achievement in a World Tour event since they joined forces at the 2026 Malaysia Masters in May.

Speaking after the match, Pang Ron admitted that he was still adapting to the pressure of playing on the big stage, saying the experience of getting through the match helped him settle into the environment.

“I feel not the best yet, but maybe a little bit too nervous. But playing for some points already, then we get used to the environment and everything. So it’s getting better and better,” he told the Badminton World Federation via an audio clip shared with the media.
Pei Jing, who was pleased with their overall performance, said the pair would now focus on developing their partnership and gradually finding a combination that suited both players. — Bernama
1eeb9e0ca6f1773b: SUNGAI BAKAP: Kerajaan memberi jaminan tiada sekolah jenis kebangsaan Tamil (SJKT) akan ditutup, kata Menteri Pendidikan Fadhlina Sidek.
Beliau berkata, sebaliknya kerajaan akan terus memberi tumpuan kepada pembangunan dan penyelenggaraan semua sekolah, selain memperkukuh program berkaitan guru serta pelajar.
“Kita memberikan jaminan sebagai kerajaan Madani, tiada SJKT yang akan ditutup.

“Malah, kita akan memberikan tumpuan kepada semua sekolah untuk pembangunan, penyelenggaraan dan juga program-program berkaitan dengan pengukuhan guru serta para pelajar kita,” katanya selepas menghadiri majlis penyerahan surat setuju terima (SST) dan pecah tanah pembinaan SJKT Sungai Bakap.
Beliau berkata, penegasan itu perlu diulangi susulan masih terdapat pandangan dalam kalangan masyarakat sekolah terbabit akan ditutup.
Dalam pada itu, Fadhlina menyifatkan pembinaan SJKT Sungai Bakap sebagai satu perkembangan yang sangat bermakna selepas melalui proses panjang.
Menurutnya, pembinaan SJKT Sungai Bakap akan dilaksanakan Yayasan Didik Negara dan mengambil masa 56 minggu.

"Pembinaan itu pula akan dipantau Jabatan Pendidikan Negeri bagi memastikan pelaksanaannya berjalan seperti ditetapkan," katanya sambil memaklumkan pembinaa SJKT Sungai Bakap melibatkan peruntukan RM12.6 juta.
f2020c08bd828366: PETALING JAYA: Entering heaven depends on Allah's permission and mercy, not on supporting any particular political party, says Amanah deputy president Mujahid Yusof Rawa.
He said the claim that joining or voting for PAS could lead to heaven was "baseless" and questioned how the party could associate its political struggle with Allah's mercy.

Mujahid was responding to PAS secretary-general Takiyuddin Hassan, who was reported to have said last night that those who joined PAS, embraced Islam and fought along the party’s principles could enter heaven.
He questioned whether a political party that labels fellow Muslims as munafik and engages in slander and lies for political power could claim to be leading people towards Allah's mercy.
Mujahid, a former religious affairs minister, said PAS appeared to be narrowing the concept of Allah's mercy by linking it to support for the party.
He called for the authorities to take appropriate action if the remarks amounted to insulting or exploiting the religion.
He said if Takiyuddin had not intended to make such a claim, the PAS leader should apologise to party members and all Muslims.
Takiyuddin had said that if someone died while fighting to defend Islam, they would be regarded as martyrs, rewarded with divine blessings and enter heaven.

He had explained that the phrase “joining PAS means entering heaven” could be seen as political opponents mocking the party, but maintained that PAS's struggle was based on Islam and aligned with teachings commanded by Allah.
“Joining PAS in that way, God willing, we can enter heaven when we die. That is certain, ladies and gentlemen,” he was quoted as saying.
Takiyuddin, who is also Kota Bharu MP and PN secretary-general, said PAS has the backing of religious scholars, including many pondok teachers, because of its commitment to an Islamic struggle.
He said PAS now has more than one million members nationwide, excluding support from non-members and overseas supporters.
“If they are taken into account, it can be said that PAS now has the support of between three and four million people.”
“This is PAS, a party that carries the call of Islam. Even its (full) name is Parti Islam Se-Malaysia, the only party that puts the word ‘Islam’ in its name,” he said.

Umno ulama council deputy chairman Khairuddin Aman Razali defended Takiyuddin, saying there was nothing wrong with the PAS secretary-general’s statement, as he was emphasising the way to attain rewards and paradise through politics.
“It is not simply joining a party that leads one to paradise, but taking part in a political struggle and pursuing aspirations aligned with Islam,” he said in a separate statement.

Khairuddin, a former PAS leader, said that if there are actions by the party, its individuals or its leaders that are not in line with Islam, then the rewards and sins should be assessed based on each specific wrongdoing.

“Such actions must be criticised and corrected from time to time because no one is immune to making mistakes. This principle also applies to any other Muslim party that champions the same cause,” he said.
11ab62a04ec41b83: NIBONG TEBAL, Sept 6 — The government has assured that no Tamil vernacular school will be closed as construction finally begins on a RM12.6 million replacement building for SJKT Sungai Bakap after nearly 17 years of delays.
Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said the Madani Government would instead continue to focus on the development and maintenance of all SJKT, as well as programmes to strengthen teachers and pupils.
She said the assurance was necessary as there were still perceptions in the community that some SJKT could be shut down.
“We give an assurance that, under the Madani Government, no SJKT will be closed.
“Instead, we will focus on all schools in terms of development, maintenance and programmes related to strengthening teachers and pupils,” she said.
Fadhlina was speaking to reporters after witnessing the groundbreaking and handover of the letter of acceptance for the new SJKT Sungai Bakap building here today.
The RM12.6 million project, to be carried out by Yayasan Didik Negara and monitored by the Penang Education Department, is expected to be completed within 56 weeks.
The new school will be built at a site about 2km from the existing location and will comprise six classrooms, special-purpose rooms and other facilities.
Fadhlina, who is also Nibong Tebal MP, said the new building was important in providing better and more comprehensive educational facilities for children in the Sungai Bakap area.
She also apologised to parents, pupils and teachers for the long wait before the project could finally be realised.
The project had been delayed since 2009 due to implementation issues, financial constraints and legal disputes, according to Bernama.
Penang special committee chairman for Tamil schools Datuk Seri S. Sundarajoo said the existing school building, which houses more than 100 pupils, was in a dilapidated condition.
He said the project had previously faced issues involving land, contractor delays and court proceedings before these were resolved.
Sundarajoo, who is also the state housing and environment executive councillor, said the state government was targeting the construction of three SJKT buildings this year.
He said SJKT Sungai Bakap was the second to be developed, while work on SJKT Juru was expected to begin before the end of the year.
0262e5028d6e8ca6: KLANG: Firemen extinguished a bush fire at Taman Eng Ann here this morning.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call at 11.05am about the fire in Jalan Murai.
"A team of seven firemen from the Klang Utara Fire and Rescue station was dispatched to the scene and arrived at 11.11am.
"The fire involved a 50ft by 30ft area of bushes.
"Firemen managed to extinguish the blaze and the operation ended at 11.36am," he said in a statement today.

The New Straits Times reported that a carelessly discarded cigarette butt, an unattended pile of burning rubbish or a small fire used to clear land could ignite a major bush or peat fire during this current hot and dry spell.
Fire and Rescue Department director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohamad said prolonged dry weather had stripped moisture from grass, bushes and other vegetation, providing ready fuel for fires.
He said hot weather was not necessarily the cause of major fires but could turn even a minor ignition source into a major blaze.
Nor Hisham said strong winds could spread flames through dry vegetation, widening the area firefighters must contain.
The warning comes following a sharp rise in open-burning incidents nationwide during the recent hot and dry spell.
Cases climbed from 53 on Aug 20 to 70 the following day before jumping to 180 on Aug 22 and peaking at 231 on Aug 23. Another 190 incidents were recorded on Aug 24.
bf93f5b28af165c1: LONDON: Prince Harry's return to Britain has reignited debate about whether taxpayers should foot the bill to protect him and his family, with experts warning genuine threats likely exist.
The Duke of Sussex, who arrived in Britain last week with his wife Meghan and their two young children, had previously ruled out returning to his home country, citing security concerns.

The couple left Britain and quit royal duties in 2020 amid a royal family feud and Harry subsequently waged a years-long, ultimately unsuccessful, legal battle to retain UK taxpayer-funded security while living in California.
Now back with their seven-year-old son, Prince Archie, and five-year-old daughter, Princess Lilibet, he has reportedly been pushing for reinstated police protection.
However, when the family landed Aug 26 at Birmingham Airport, they had private security in place rather than police officers, according to British media.
"It's very surprising," Scott Hamer, an ex-protection officer for Harry's father King Charles III when he was Prince of Wales, told AFP.
"There's probably people who are being protected now who are at less threat and risk than he is. So the question would be, why does he not receive that protection as well?"
'Vulnerability'
Harry and Meghan, who are reportedly living in central England's Cotswolds region, are said to have enrolled their children at private schools there for the coming academic year.
They are thought to have heightened concerns about security around the kids' daily drop-off and collection, given that these follow predictable patterns.
"The vulnerability aspect needs to be assessed," said Hamer.
"The fact that he'll have to take his kids to school at the same time each day, and pick them up at the same time each day, now makes him quite vulnerable," Hamer said.
Britain's Royal and VIP Executive Committee (Ravec) - an independent body overseen by the interior ministry - decides which politicians, royals and others get police protection.
Harry battled the ministry in the courts after Ravec downgraded his security following his 2020 North America move.
The prince lost his bid to reverse the decision, branding the 2025 dismissal of his appeal a "good old-fashioned Establishment stitch-up".
With his return, Ravec's risk management board will likely be re-evaluating the threat level he faces.
"It's very real," explained Hamer, noting it could range from international terrorism to extreme right-wing actors opposed to his marriage to mixed-race Meghan.
'Threat'
The Sunday Times reported last week that Harry's lawyers wrote to interior minister Shabana Mahmood in August requesting she intervene.
The paper said he had lost faith in Ravec's ability to rule fairly on his security needs, citing sources close to him.
A government spokesman said the protection system was "rigorous and proportionate" while noting its long-standing policy not to provide details of arrangements.
"Doing so could compromise their integrity and affect individuals security," the spokesperson added.
Harry is thought to be pushing for police protection in part because private security in the UK cannot be armed.

"That's what his argument is: that the threat against him is so great that it can only be dealt with [through] an official police protection team," another former royal protection officer, Simon Morgan, told AFP. "He feels that he should get it."
However, the British public appear to think otherwise.
Just 6% say the prince's security should be fully taxpayer-funded while 63 percent believe the couple should pay for it, according to a poll last week for The i Paper.
"He's paid for security in the States. I can't see why he can't pay for security here -- it's a lot less dangerous," royal expert Andrew Lownie told AFP.
'Lot of money'
Hamer said whether Harry was a working royal or not "shouldn't be part of it," noting ex-PMs get protected despite leaving office.
Lownie predicted Harry would succeed in getting some taxpayer-funded protection reinstated for the same reason.
However, he noted the bill for such services has ballooned over the last decade, which has seen six prime ministers leave office - compared to just two in the prior 10 years.
"If we're doing it for all these prime ministers, then I think we're going to have to do it for Harry and his family. But that is going to cost a lot of money," he said.
Harry has consistently argued he and his family are at increased risk given he is the king's son and due to his UK military service.
The prince completed two tours of Afghanistan and claimed in his explosive 2023 memoir "Spare" to have killed 25 Taliban fighters.
Choosing to make the high-profile admission prompted criticism at the time from some British veterans, who noted it could increase his personal security risk.
0c730195b093695b: ISKANDAR PUTERI: More than 600 Orang Asli youths are currently pursuing their studies at universities and colleges nationwide, reflecting the government's concern over education issues affecting the community.

Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the figure had exceeded the initial target of 200 when the Department of Orang Asli Development (Jakoa) was placed under the Rural and Regional Development Ministry, which he heads, four years ago.
"In the first year, the challenge was accepted. It was not just 200 entering universities, but more than 300 Orang Asli youths enrolled in universities that year.
"In the second year, I raised the target to 300.

"Clearly, the achievement of Orang Asli youths entering universities increased to 400 in the second year," he said when officiating the closing ceremony of the 2026 National Orang Asli Sports Carnival at the EduCity Sports Complex here today.
Also present was Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi.
Zahid said the achievement of more than 600 students this year proved that the Orang Asli community had the ability to progress further if given the opportunity and appropriate educational support.
"This is good social mobility because education is an element that can improve the social status of any community in the world," he said.

He said efforts to empower education among the Orang Asli community had also been expanded to Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), including through the provision of specialised institutions for the community.
Zahid said one such institution was the Paya Bungor Training Centre in Maran, Pahang, which currently has 135 Orang Asli youths enrolled in TVET programmes offering both short and long-term courses.
He also commended the Johor government's commitment to allocating RM600,000 to 60 Orang Asli villages in the state, equivalent to RM10,000 for each village.
d964eb351adc64ce: SINGAPORE, Sept 6 — Chinese food delivery giant Meituan has denied offering cross-border delivery services after a viral video showed a man in its signature yellow uniform claiming he had been flown to Singapore to buy just S$13.50 (RM43) worth of curry puffs.
Singapore-based Chinese-language newspaper Lianhe Zaobao reported yesterday that Meituan had not launched any international food delivery or errand service.
A customer service representative contacted through the Meituan app said customers could not place orders in China and have a rider fly to Singapore to collect food.
The representative stressed that Meituan does not support such arrangements and provides no cross-border delivery service.

The denial came after a video posted on Chinese social media platform Xiaohongshu showed a man wearing what appeared to be a Meituan jacket and helmet buying six curry puffs at Paya Lebar Quarter Mall.
Speaking to the person filming him, the man claimed that a customer had spent about 2,400 yuan, or S$450, to fly him to Singapore for the errand.
His supposed mission was to pick up a box of six curry puffs from Hong Lim Curry Puff, including curry potato and sardine flavours, costing just S$13.50.
He did not reveal who the customer was or how much he had been paid for carrying out the unusual assignment.
The incident took place on August 31.
Hong Lim Curry Puff founder Victoria Loh, 37, said a part-time employee who does not speak Mandarin called her for help when the man arrived at the outlet.
When Loh reached the shop, the man asked whether he could pay using WeChat Pay or Alipay, two payment platforms widely used in China.
The shop could not accept either method.
Loh said she initially assumed he was a “normal” customer and told her employee to proceed “as usual”.
She only realised something unusual was happening after hearing a woman, identified as the Xiaohongshu user filming the video, shout: “Meituan!”
3d64d6d933898fd6: BENGALURU: OPEC+ is set to keep its oil output policy unchanged for October at a meeting on Sunday, two people familiar with the discussions told Reuters, as the producer group needs to agree on new quotas before deciding its next output steps.

The meeting comes as the Iran war continues to disrupt oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz, limiting OPEC+'s influence over prices and market share. Unlike in the past, the group's supply decisions have had a limited impact on the market.
In August, OPEC+ agreed to increase production in September, completing a phased rollback of a 1.65 million-barrel-per-day supply cut first agreed in 2023.

Despite the agreed production increases, the group, made up of the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and its allies, including Russia, still produces far below its targets because of the war.
OPEC+ still has another layer of production cuts in place, covering most members of the 21-country group until the end of 2026.
Before the group decides how to unwind the cuts and return production to the market, it needs to review members' oil production capacity to set 2027 output baselines, which form the basis for quotas.
This debate will likely happen later in 2026, and hence OPEC+ is likely to pause its output increases for the fourth quarter, sources earlier told Reuters.
7ba4563c39442221: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — Malaysia Airlines and Batik Air have cancelled a total of 20 flights between Malaysia and Jakarta today after volcanic ash from the ongoing eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau disrupted operations at Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport (CGK).

Malaysia Airlines said in its post on X that it would cancel 12 flights between Kuala Lumpur (KUL) and Jakarta (CGK), namely MH713, MH712, MH711, MH710, MH717, MH716, MH721, MH720, MH723, MH722, MH725 and MH724.
“Given the evolving situation, Malaysia Airlines is closely monitoring developments.
“Further updates on affected flights will be communicated directly to affected customers,” it said.
The national carrier reminded passengers to ensure their contact details are up to date via “My Booking” on its website to receive timely updates by email and SMS.
Customers may also contact its Live Chat support on the Malaysia Airlines website or its Global Contact Centre for assistance.
“The safety of our passengers and crew remains our utmost priority,” it added.
Meanwhile, Batik Air said in a separate statement that it had cancelled eight scheduled flights between Malaysia and Jakarta today, namely OD398, OD399, OD346, OD347, OD388, OD389, OD390 and OD391.
Six of the cancelled services operate between Kuala Lumpur International Airport and Jakarta, while two operate between Subang and Jakarta.
It said the decision followed close coordination with aviation authorities and airport operators, reflecting its commitment to the safety and wellbeing of passengers and crew.
“The presence of volcanic ash in the airspace can reduce visibility, interfere with aircraft navigation systems, and potentially compromise engine performance,” it said.
Batik Air said it would continue to monitor the situation and provide updates on flight operations to and from the affected destinations through its official website and social media channels.
Affected passengers would also be notified through their registered contact details.
“Affected passengers may request to reschedule their travel to the next available Batik Air flight, subject to availability, or request a refund.
“Passengers are advised to contact Batik Air’s Customer Care Centre or their respective booking channels for assistance with their preferred option,” it said.
Batik Air, a Malaysian carrier, operates under Indonesia’s Lion Air Group. — Bernama
3d4d1aae0cfd0177: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim contacted former United States vice-president Al Gore to discuss the global climate crisis and Malaysia's efforts to mitigate its environmental impact.
Anwar said they also discussed the haze affecting Malaysia following forest fires in Indonesia.
"The discussion also covered Malaysia's commitment and ongoing measures to accelerate the country's energy transition from fossil fuels to cleaner, more sustainable energy sources.

"These efforts are in line with the government's commitment to building a country that is progressive and economically resilient, while preserving environmental sustainability for the well-being of future generations," he said in a Facebook post.

Anwar added that he had invited Gore to visit Malaysia soon to continue discussions and explore avenues for closer cooperation on tackling climate change and advancing the country's energy transition agenda.
fb8a06fead440a22: KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional (BN) should push for the 16th general election (GE16) to be held as soon as possible to restore political stability, said the People's Progressive Party (PPP).

Its president, Datuk Dr Loga Bala Mohan, said the country was already experiencing "election fever" following the recent elections in Johor and Negeri Sembilan, with the Melaka election expected to be next.

"We are seeing a lot of instability, and this needs to be addressed before things get out of hand. We urge BN to seek to have the general election held as soon as possible," he told reporters after chairing the party's Supreme Council meeting at its headquarters today.
Recently, Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi voiced support for an earlier GE16, saying it would allow the government to seek a fresh mandate.
Zahid, who is also BN chairman, said the coalition was nevertheless prepared to face the polls if Parliament served its full term.
The 15th Parliament is due to complete its full term on Dec 18 next year.
Meanwhile, Loga Bala said he hoped the government would consider the higher costs involved in holding state elections separately from the general election.
"This involves taxpayers' money. If the elections are held simultaneously, the cost can be reduced," he said.
He said holding the elections simultaneously would also be in line with the Madani government's previous pledge to reduce wastage in the use of public funds.
"Reducing the cost of elections is one way this can be achieved," he said.
02195c588ca64d8e: LUMUT: Budget 2027 is expected to place particular emphasis on efforts to address socioeconomic issues, including the welfare of the middle-income (M40) and lower-income groups, according to an aide of the Finance Minister.

Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim, who is political secretary to Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, said the focus on both groups was necessary as they are among those most affected by economic pressures and current cost-of-living challenges.

"The Budget to be announced by the Prime Minister will be another more inclusive Budget, one that is closer to the people and can, to some extent, resolve several problems and issues that have arisen.
"For now, the parties involved are still conducting direct engagement sessions with all stakeholders to finalise the Budget," he said.

He said this when met after officiating the National Khatam Keris Traditional Ceremony organised by the Perak branch of the Persatuan Silat Seni Gayong Malaysia and the Silat Anak-Anak Gayong Perak Gathering at Teluk Batik Campsite here today.
Anwar, who is Prime Minister and Finance Minister, is scheduled to table Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat on Oct 9.
Muhammad Kamil said existing initiatives such as the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) would continue to be strengthened to ease the financial burden on households.
"Assistance programmes such as STR and SARA will continue, and we await further announcements by the Finance Minister," he said.
Muhammad Kamil said consideration was also being given to proposals to improve existing initiatives and introduce other forms of financial support to ease the burden on middle-income households.
"The government's priorities also remain focused on ensuring that political and economic stability remains strong to guarantee the smooth implementation of national policies," he said.
a4fedc872380df73: SINGAPORE, Sept 6 — A 20-year-old Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) full-time national serviceman has died after being found unconscious while on duty at Marina Bay Fire Station, less than a month after completing his firefighter training.
Lance Corporal Muhammad Nur Ilham Mohammed Iswadi was found in the station’s training yard at about 8.10am today, Singapore-based media organisation CNA reported, citing an SCDF statement.
SCDF personnel immediately performed cardiopulmonary resuscitation before he was taken to Singapore General Hospital.
“He was subsequently conveyed to Singapore General Hospital, where he passed away,” SCDF said.

Muhammad Nur Ilham had enlisted on February 10 and completed his firefighter course at the Civil Defence Academy on August 7. He was posted to Marina Bay Fire Station on August 18, less than three weeks before his death.
Police said preliminary investigations did not suggest foul play.
“A 20-year-old man was conveyed unconscious to the hospital, where he subsequently passed away. Based on preliminary investigations, the police do not suspect foul play,” police said.
SCDF said it was “saddened by his death” and extended its “deepest condolences to his family”.
“We are providing all necessary assistance and support to the family during this difficult time,” the force said.
61de30c65382ebe9: ISKANDAR PUTERI: The cloud seeding operation was extended across Sarawak to help improve air quality following the haze enveloping several parts of the state.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said two divisions, Kuching and Sri Aman, recorded very unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of this morning.

He, who is also National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) chairman, said the situation in Serian, which was declared a state of emergency yesterday, had begun to show positive developments, with API readings continuing to decline.
"We hope that in conjunction with the Malaysia Day celebrations in Kuching, the cloud seeding operations will help lower the air pollution index, particularly in Sarawak."
Zahid, who is also rural and regional development minister, said this after attending the closing ceremony of the 2026 National Orang Asli Sports Carnival at the Educity Sports Complex here today.
Earlier, Nadma director-general Datuk Meor Ismail Meor Akim had said that cloud seeding operations were being carried out across Sarawak until tomorrow to mitigate the haze affecting the state.

His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, the King of Malaysia, on Friday consented to declaring a state of emergency throughout the Serian division after the area recorded hazardous API readings of more than 500 at the time.
However, checks showed that Serian recorded an unhealthy API reading of 183 as of 3.15pm today.

According to the Environment Department's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), 35 other air quality monitoring stations, including 10 in Sarawak, also recorded API readings in the same category.
Only Kuching recorded a very unhealthy API reading, at 218.
8a22cfbdcda55e0e: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — Five Malaysian volunteers are heading deep into one of Nepal’s worst-hit flood zones, travelling over rough terrain to deliver emergency supplies and help families whose homes and communities have been devastated by floods and landslides.

The team from United Sikhs Malaysia, a Malaysian humanitarian aid organisation involved in disaster relief and community assistance, is travelling to Dhunche in Rasuwa district to establish a base camp before pushing on to Syapru Besi near the Nepal-Tibet border.

In a Facebook post today, the group said that the journey to Dhunche is expected to take 10 to 12 hours, with the team then facing challenging off-road conditions to reach Syapru Besi, about 40km from the border.
The volunteers will first unload relief supplies at their base before continuing to the affected town.
The team’s immediate priority is to build temporary shelters for families displaced by the disaster, the group’s legal director Raspreet Kaur told the The New Straits Times.
She said a local resident had also sought help for 98 children whose parents remained missing, with the team planning to provide necessities including colouring materials.
The volunteers had earlier prepared mosquito nets and tarpaulins worth about RM28,000 for around 300 affected families, with the supplies delivered to a gurdwara in Kathmandu.
United Sikhs Malaysia said Team A is expected to remain in Nepal for about two weeks, while additional teams are on standby depending on the situation on the ground.
United Sikhs Malaysia’s mission comes as other Malaysian teams and organisations are also responding to the disaster.

Mercy Malaysia has deployed a humanitarian assessment team to Nepal to assess conditions on the ground and identify urgent needs, including emergency shelter, food, clean water, sanitation and healthcare.

Malaysia has also sent 11 officers and personnel from the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) to assist with search-and-rescue operations in areas affected by the floods and landslides.
The 10-day SMART mission is expected to include operations in areas where people may still be trapped, while the team will also assist in efforts to locate Malaysians affected by the disaster.
The Malaysian government has also pledged US$1 million (RM4.2 million) to help Nepal’s disaster victims and support recovery efforts.
The disaster has particularly disrupted access to communities in Rasuwa, where flooding and landslides have damaged roads, bridges and other infrastructure, making relief operations difficult.
a27e37a224c913f3: PUTRAJAYA: Bekalan bahan api Malaysia masih kukuh walaupun paras bekalan global berada dalam paras rendah, kerajaan yakin negara ini akan memperoleh bekalan yang mencukupi sehingga akhir tahun, kata Penasihat Ekonomi Perdana Menteri Nurhisham Hussein.
Nurhisham, yang juga mengetuai Sekretariat Pasukan Petugas Pengurusan Krisis Majlis Tindakan Ekonomi Negara (MTEN) berkata situasi bahan api global kekal stabil.
Risiko, bagaimanapun, kekal condong ke arah harga yang lebih tinggi berikutan ketegangan geopolitik dan gangguan terhadap laluan perkapalan utama, katanya.
Walaupun Malaysia merupakan pengeksport bersih gas asli cecair (LNG) ia tetap menjadi pengimport utama minyak mentah.

Bekalan minyak global telah terjejas akibat konflik di Asia Barat, yang meletus pada Februari lepas dan tidak menunjukkan tanda-tanda akan berakhir, dengan serangan masih berterusan antara Amerika Syarikat dan Iran sehingga ke hari ini.
Nurhisham berkata kebanyakan negara mungkin akan membina semula rizab minyak mereka hanya apabila harga kembali ke paras yang lebih munasabah iaitu sekitar US$80 setong.

“Jadi, kita akan mempunyai pembinaan semula rizab yang sangat perlahan oleh negara-negara ini, tetapi ini juga membayangkan bahawa dalam tempoh dua hingga tiga tahun akan datang harga minyak akan terus berada di aras tertinggi.
“Ia mungkin tidak melonjak tetapi akan terus naik. Dari segi bahan api, keadaan semasa masih lagi stabil,” katanya pada taklimat media mengenai krisis bekalan global baru-baru ini.

Terusan Suez dan Bab-el-Mandeb masih dibuka walaupun terdapat ancaman yang berterusan, manakala kerosakan kemudahan di Rusia dan sekatan Amerika Syarikat terhadap eksport Iran juga antara faktor yang boleh menjejaskan bekalan minyak global.
Beliau berkata kehabisan rizab akhirnya akan menghapuskan satu sumber bekalan dan ini akan menambah ketidaktentuan dalam pasaran tenaga global.
425371118081347b: Women passengers should have option to choose female e-hailing drivers — Loke
PUTRAJAYA: E-hailing companies are encouraged to offer female driver options for women passengers to improve their safety and comfort, says Transport Minister Anthony Loke.
He said the option would give women passengers an alternative that prioritised their well-being when using e-hailing services.

"This is a feature that I hope our women leaders can promote. When using e-hailing services, one of the available options should be the ability to choose a female driver," he said in his speech at the Wanita DAP National Congress 2026 here today, in his capacity as the party's secretary-general.
Loke said he had also urged e-hailing companies to introduce women-only carpooling options.
"I suggested that carpooling should include a women-only option, allowing female passengers to share rides only with other women," he said.

On rail services, Loke said safety measures continued to be strengthened through women-only coaches following frequent complaints to the ministry about sexual harassment, particularly during peak hours.
He said women accounted for nearly two-thirds of rail passengers, making their safety a priority.
Meanwhile, Loke said efforts to empower women in the transport sector included creating more opportunities in traditionally male-dominated fields such as aviation and maritime.
He said gender stereotypes in these sectors must be challenged to ensure women were given opportunities based on their abilities.
"We believe that if men can fly aircraft, women can do the same. If women can drive, why can't they fly aircraft? These stereotypes must be changed," he said.
eb824b07a659c142: KUCHING: Cloud seeding operations across Sarawak have been extended until tomorrow as efforts continue to mitigate transboundary haze affecting the state.

Sarawak Disaster Management Committee (SDMC) chairman Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas said the extension followed a successful operation yesterday, which brought rainfall to the targeted areas around Bakun and Murum dams.
"Today's operation will continue as planned and will be carried out where suitable cloud and weather conditions permit," he said in a statement today.
Sarawak has been conducting cloud seeding operations targeting key dams and water catchment areas in the state since Thursday.
Meanwhile, Uggah said air quality in Serian had shown an improving trend, with the air pollutant index (API) reading at 185 as at noon today, placing it in the unhealthy category.
"There is a downward trend for the API level in Serian as we enter the second of three days of monitoring. The API is primarily affected by wind direction and the source of hotspots," he said.

He said continued monitoring was necessary before any formal recommendation on Serian's emergency status could be submitted to Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Uggah said data from the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) showed there were no hotspots in Sarawak, while 184 were detected in neighbouring Kalimantan, Indonesia.

a08330300ec8990c: PETALING JAYA: Pertubuhan Jaringan Insan Madani (Perjim) today successfully organised the Muhibbah Ride cycling event as part of its Merdeka Day and Malaysia Day celebrations.
The NGO’s chairman, Aidi Amin, said the Muhibbah Ride was one of Perjim's many initiatives to promote a healthier lifestyle both physically and mentally.
"Racial harmony and a healthy life are deeply connected, as inner peace and community well-being depend on living free from hatred and division," he said in a statement.
The Muhibbah Ride involved various cycling groups and more than 250 cyclists taking part in a 73km journey around Paya Jaras, Sungai Buloh.
Aidi said unity in a multiracial society is often marred by “menacing individuals”, and every Malaysian bears the duty to preserve harmony by engaging more with their community.

He also said it is important for Malaysians to remind themselves of the spirit of muhibbah - friendship, camaraderie, and mutual understanding among people from different racial, cultural and religious backgrounds.
"You can never backpedal on a bike, and we must always move forward in our journey together as a nation. Always look ahead against all odds," he said.
d4448f0311b81a04: SHAH ALAM: Four sports events at the Selangor Para Malaysia Games (Sukma) have been postponed after the Air Pollutant Index (API) reached an unhealthy 169 at noon today.

Organising committee deputy chairman Mohd Najwan Halimi said the decision followed advice from the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), the Selangor State Health Department, and a technical committee monitoring the haze.
"The API readings in Shah Alam and Klang reached an unhealthy level of 169 as of noon today.

"This has forced the us to postpone four sports: athletics at the UiTM Stadium; swimming at the Selangor Aquatics Complex; archery at the Selangor State Youth and Sports Complex; and lawn bowls at Bayuemas, Klang," he said in a statement.
Najwan said updates on the events will be announced based on ongoing API readings in affected areas.
The Selangor Para Sukma began yesterday.
Athletics, powerlifting, archery, badminton, boccia, table tennis, chess, and lawn bowls were held earlier today. - Bernama
3bd4bf9553a8c158: BERLIN, Sept 6 — German voters headed to the polls today for a crucial regional election in the ex-communist east where the far-right, anti-immigration and Moscow-friendly AfD is expected to win easily.
The Alternative for Germany, polling at over 40 per cent for months in Saxony-Anhalt, even has its sights on winning its first-ever state government, although this is far from assured.
Polls opened at 8am local time (0600 GMT) and some 1.7 million voters have until 6pm (1600 GMT) to cast their ballots, with first projections expected shortly after.

The small state is now ruled by the centre-right CDU of Chancellor Friedrich Merz in coalition with two smaller parties, and its state premier Sven Schulze hopes to build again a multi-party coalition to cling to power.

All other major parties have so far maintained a “firewall” of non-cooperation with the AfD, whose Saxony-Anhalt branch is categorised as “right-wing extremist” by Germany’s domestic intelligence agency.

The AfD’s top candidate Ulrich Siegmund — a telegenic 35-year-old who is feted like a rock star at campaign events and has a large social media following — has confidently predicted gaining an absolute majority.
“It was the others who erected the firewalls,” he told Bild daily. “If no one wants to work with us, then we’ll just have to do it alone.”
Such a scenario would shake Germany, a country that has long been at pains to atone for its dark history in World War II and the Holocaust and which has so far kept extremist parties in check.
A strong AfD win would also heap pressure on Merz, who has vowed to reboot a stagnant economy and restrict irregular immigration, but has seen his party beaten by the AfD in national surveys too.

“If the AfD wins in Saxony-Anhalt, Merz’s critics will become even more vocal, and calls for better leadership will become impossible to ignore,” said political scientist Wolfgang Schroeder of Kassel University.
However, Schroeder also said he does not expect Merz to be ousted, given the current absence of a strong rival candidate: “As far as I can see, there is no alternative chancellor.”
‘Remigration and deportation offensive’
Siegmund has vowed to topple a “domino” today and lead a political revolution from the small state of 2.1 million people that propels the anti-establishment party to national victory in 2029.
The AfD’s key campaign promises include a “remigration and deportation offensive”, a ban on LGBTQ pride rainbow flags at public schools, and an end to new wind farms.
The party has also tapped into a sense of nostalgia for communist East Germany and lingering resentment about an enduring wealth gap with the West decades after the 1989 fall of the Berlin Wall.
The prospect of an AfD state government — while eagerly awaited by many voters — has sparked alarm among mainstream parties and minority groups.
Thousands of the AfD’s opponents joined a “festival of democracy” rally in Magdeburg on the eve of the vote.
The German Economic Institute warned the AfD’s immigration policy would be “ruinous” for the state, whose population is already ageing, shrinking and highly reliant on foreign-born workers.
Others have voiced fears an AfD-run state security apparatus could leak sensitive information to Russia.

The Kremlin “makes no secret of the fact that the AfD is the most important instrument for destabilising Germany for (Russian President Vladimir) Putin,” Thuringia state interior minister Georg Maier told the Handelsblatt daily.
The latest poll, released Thursday by public broadcaster ZDF, gave the AfD a commanding lead of 41 per cent.
The CDU got 23 per cent, the centre-left SPD 8.5 per cent and the Greens six per cent, while two smaller parties failed to cross the 5 per cent hurdle to reenter parliament.
A similar result may allow a scenario where the CDU and others form a minority government with ad hoc support from the far-left Die Linke party, which polled at 11.5 per cent.
In the final stretch of campaigning, a social media video stoked fears about mail vote fraud, with claims of manipulation at an elderly care home that were denied by state authorities.
Germany’s parliamentary speaker Julia Kloeckner dismissed AfD speculation of voter manipulation, speaking to news weekly Der Spiegel.
“Questioning elections without concrete evidence appears to have one goal,” she said, “to sow distrust in our rules and to accept the results only if the outcome suits”. — AFP
5b64b50a4b737650: PETALING JAYA: Malaysian mixed doubles pair Hoo Pang Ron-Lai Pei Jing came agonisingly close to making history at the China Masters, falling short in the final against China's world No 1 duo Feng Yan Zhe-Huang Dong Ping.
World No 85 Pang Ron-Pei Jing, who were hoping to be the first Malaysian shuttlers to ever win a title at the China Masters since its inception in 2005, went down 19-21, 16-21 in 49 minutes.

Their runner-up finish at the Sports Centre Gymnasium in Shenzhen, China, marked their first-ever final at a Super 750 tournament — a remarkable achievement for a partnership that has been together for just four months.

The Malaysian duo had beaten much higher-ranked pairs in all their matches en route to the final. They are expected to jump several places higher with this performance when the Badminton World Federation (BWF) releases the new ranking list on Tuesday.
For Pang Ron, this was his second runner-up title at one of the BWF’s top-tier tournaments.
In 2024, he partnered Cheng Su Yin to enter the China Masters final and also lost to Yan Zhe-Dong Ping in three games. Last year, Malaysia’s Chen Tang Jie-Toh Ee Wei were also runners-up.
6f76d870f0c7216d: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Sept 6 — Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today urged political parties to put talk of who could become prime minister after the 16th general election aside for now, saying the focus should instead be on the upcoming Melaka state election.

The Umno president said it was too early to name or discuss a potential prime ministerial candidate when the timing of Parliament’s dissolution and the next general election remained unknown, Harian Metro reported.
“It is too early to put forward someone or a particular figure to hold that position because the election could still be far away or it could be otherwise.

“We do not know when Parliament will be dissolved. I think it is better that we put that aside for now and focus on facing the Melaka state election,” he was quoted as saying after the closing of the 2026 National Orang Asli Sports Carnival at the EduCity Sports Complex here.
Zahid, who is also deputy prime minister, said attention should remain on the Melaka election before any discussions on federal-level political matters take place.
On cooperation among political parties for the Melaka election, he said this would only be decided after the Melaka Legislative Assembly was dissolved.

His remarks came after PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang said the party had a potential prime ministerial candidate from among its leaders for GE16, but that it was not yet time to reveal the individual.
He made the remarks at PAS’ annual congress in Kota Bharu, Kelantan last Friday.
a6b17cdde2c2e754: SHAH ALAM, Sept 6 — The Selangor 2026 Malaysia Games (Sukma) and Para Sukma Organising Committee today postponed four para sports events after the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading reached an unhealthy level of 169 as of noon.

Organising Committee deputy chairman Mohd Najwan Halimi said the decision was made following advice from the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), the Selangor State Health Department and a special technical committee which has been monitoring the situation from time to time.
“The API readings in Shah Alam and Klang as of noon today showed an unhealthy level of 169.

0b060ad6b3066021: NEW YORK, Sept 6 — Defending champion Carlos Alcaraz will be under the microscope again today taking on 20th-seeded American Tommy Paul for a place in the US Open quarter-finals.

The Spaniard, playing his first tournament since a four-month absence with a wrist injury, acknowledges he has yet to play his best but says he’s “getting there” with both the sharpness of his shots and his on-court decision making.

He headlines a day that also features women’s two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka and third-ranked American Jessica Pegula — just one of the players with a chance to supplant Sabalenka atop the world rankings in New York.

Surprise Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova will try to continue her progress toward another Grand Slam against dangerous Ukrainian Marta Kostyuk while US hope Frances Tiafoe faces the always tricky former champion Daniil Medvedev.
AFP Sport looks at three matches to watch on Day 8 of the US Open:
Tommy Paul (USA x20) v Carlos Alcaraz (ESP x2)
Alcaraz leads head-to-head 6-2
Although Alcaraz has dominated their meetings — Paul’s last win over the Spaniard was back in 2023 — the defending champion said the American is “really dangerous for everyone on the tour.

“The way he plays, the way he hits the ball, it’s really complicated to dominate the ball, dominate the points,” said Alcaraz, who won their last meeting in the Australian open quarter-finals on the way to the title that made him the youngest man to claim a career Grand Slam.
Alcaraz said he was looking forward to another great battle — and having some fun.
“We pull off great points, great shots,” he said. “It’s going to be really fun to watch, fun to play, as well.”
Ben Shelton (USA X8) v Stefanos Tsitsipas (GRE)
Tsitsipas leads head-to-head 1-0

A resurgent Tsitsipas has Shelton’s attention. The former top-five player from Greece upset red-hot Arthur Fils in the first round and ousted 18th-seeded Jiri Lehecka in the third and is deeper into a Grand Slam than he’s been in more than two years.
Playing pain free after back problems derailed his 2025 campaign, the two-time Grand Slam finalist is also working with a new coach, having replaced his father Apostolos in that role.
“I have been watching his matches,” Shelton said. “I think he’s playing great. I think that his style of tennis can be very, very effective on all surfaces, all-court game, great athlete.”
Shelton said his three four-set wins in the first three rounds — against Tallon Griekspoor, Hubert Hurkacz and Denis Shapovalov — had him well prepared for anything Tsitsipas might throw at him.

“I think this is a great way to start the tournament in terms of variety. I have dealt with a lefty, dealt with a big hitter, dealt with a feel guy, dealt with a massive server, dealt with a spot server, serve and volleyer.”
Aryna Sabalenka (BLR x1) v Taylor Townsend (USA)
First meeting
Sabalenka knows she’ll be in hostile territory when she takes on 96th-ranked American Townsend on Arthur Ashe Stadium.
“I think I’m ready for the crowd situation,” Sabalenka said. “She’s, I’d say, tricky player, because she brings the variety — comes to the net, really make you think during the game.”

Townsend is in the fourth round for a second straight year, but it has been anything but a straightforward 12 months for the 30-year-old, who says she has “been through a lot over this past year.” It hasn’t dimmed her desire to win, and Townsend said she was “pumped” to take on Sabalenka in a quest for a first Grand Slam singles quarter-final.
“I’m built for these moments,” Townsend, a three-time Grand Slam doubles winner, said. “I’m ready to take it. I’m ready to go.” — AFP

0fd9797e4b503b00: JAKARTA: Empat lagi lapangan terbang di Indonesia ditutup sementara pada Ahad susulan abu gunung berapi daripada letusan Anak Krakatau yang terus merebak, sekali gus menjejaskan operasi penerbangan dan menjadikan keseluruhan lima lapangan terbang terjejas.

Ketua Pengarah Penerbangan Awam Kementerian Pengangkutan, Lukman F Laisa, berkata penutupan tambahan itu melibatkan Lapangan Terbang Halim Perdanakusuma di Jakarta, Lapangan Terbang Raden Inten II di Lampung, Lapangan Terbang Budiarto di Curug dan Lapangan Terbang Pondok Cabe.
“Jadi, lima lapangan terbang ditutup. Kami terus memantau pergerakan abu ini,” katanya dalam sidang media secara dalam talian pada Ahad.

Beliau berkata kementerian sedang menyelaras dengan pengendali lapangan terbang, AirNav Indonesia serta Badan Meteorologi, Klimatologi dan Geofizik (BMKG) berhubung perkembangan pergerakan abu gunung berapi itu.
Terdahulu, pihak berkuasa memaklumkan Lapangan Terbang Antarabangsa Soekarno-Hatta ditutup sementara sejak 1.30 pagi Ahad selepas abu gunung berapi dikesan di kawasan lapangan terbang itu.
Tempoh penutupan lapangan terbang berkenaan dilanjutkan sehingga 1.30 tengah hari waktu tempatan.
Sementara itu, Lapangan Terbang Halim Perdanakusuma, Raden Inten II dan Pondok Cabe dijadual kekal ditutup sehingga 2 petang, manakala Lapangan Terbang Budiarto sehingga 1.30 tengah hari.

Anak Krakatau yang terletak di Selat Sunda antara Jawa dan Sumatera kekal pada Tahap III (Siaga) sejak 2 Julai, iaitu tahap kedua tertinggi dalam sistem amaran gunung berapi empat tahap Indonesia, dengan zon larangan sejauh tiga kilometer dikuatkuasakan di sekitar gunung berapi itu.

BMKG dalam kenyataan memaklumkan analisis satelit pada 8 pagi Ahad mengesan dua kelompok abu gunung berapi yang meliputi Banten, Jakarta dan Jawa Barat serta meluas hingga ke Bengkulu, manakala amaran penerbangan terbaharunya menunjukkan abu mencecah ketinggian sehingga 20,000 kaki (6,096 meter) dan bergerak ke arah timur serta sehingga 50,000 kaki (15,240 meter) ke arah barat.

Pengarah Gempa Bumi dan Tsunami Dr Wilya Yanto dalam sidang media sama berkata aktiviti letusan berterusan termasuk lontaran lava berulang kali masih diperhatikan pada pagi Ahad, meskipun kekerapannya semakin berkurangan.

Dalam sidang media berasingan, Ketua Badan Geologi Indonesia Lana Saria berkata letusan berulang dan berterusan menunjukkan bekalan magma dan gas di dalam gunung berapi itu masih berlaku, namun menegaskan bahawa letusan yang kerap tidak semestinya menandakan letusan lebih besar akan berlaku.

Beliau berkata aktiviti seismik dan gegaran masih direkodkan, menunjukkan pergerakan atau pelepasan bendalir gunung berapi dalam sistem berkenaan, manakala masa, magnitud dan bentuk letusan seterusnya tidak dapat ditentukan dengan tepat.

Mengenai kemungkinan tsunami, Lana berkata bukan setiap letusan Anak Krakatau akan mencetuskan tsunami, sambil menjelaskan bahawa tsunami Selat Sunda pada 22 Dis 2018 berpunca terutamanya daripada keruntuhan sebahagian besar struktur gunung berapi itu ke dalam laut.

“Berdasarkan penilaian setakat ini, struktur gunung berapi yang terbentuk semula selepas 22 Dis 2018 masih relatif kecil dan tidak dianggap berupaya runtuh pada skala yang boleh mencetuskan tsunami,” katanya sambil menambah perubahan aktiviti dan morfologi gunung berapi itu terus dipantau rapi.

Ketua Badan Nasional Penanggulangan Bencana (BNPB) Suharyanto berkata operasi modifikasi cuaca akan dilaksanakan pada Ahad hingga petang bagi membantu mengurangkan kesan abu gunung berapi yang menjejaskan Jakarta dan kawasan sekitarnya.

Sementara itu, Menteri Kesihatan Budi Gunadi Sadikin berkata kementerian telah mengaktifkan Pusat Operasi Kecemasan Kesihatan dan akan mengeluarkan garis panduan terperinci kepada petugas kesihatan di daerah dan bandar yang terjejas.

Beliau berkata abu gunung berapi boleh menyebabkan masalah pernafasan, mata dan kulit serta menasihatkan penduduk di kawasan terjejas supaya berada di dalam rumah jika boleh dan memakai pelitup muka serta cermin mata sekiranya perlu keluar, manakala pusat kesihatan masyarakat telah dilengkapi dengan nebuliser dan alat pemekat oksigen, ubat titis mata serta salap kulit.

998229ccb17a4eb4: PETALING JAYA: The drop in fuel supply levels globally has no impact on Malaysia as the fuel supply here remains stable, according to the Prime Minister’s economic adviser Nurhisham Hussein
He said the government was also confident it could secure sufficient supplies until the end of the year, Bernama reported.

“Petronas is confident that we'll be able to (have enough supply) through the end of the year (and) that they'll be able to get supplies,” he told a media briefing on the global supply crisis on Friday.
Nurhisham, who also heads the Secretariat of the National Economic Action Council (MTEN) crisis management task force, said the global fuel situation has remained fluid.
"Risks, however, remained skewed towards higher prices due to geopolitical tensions and disruptions to key shipping routes," he added.
Malaysia is a major importer of crude oil but is a net exporter of liquefied natural gas (LNG).

Global oil supplies have been severely affected due to the West Asia conflict, which erupted in February and has shown no signs of ending, with continued attacks between the United States and Iran until today.
Nurhisham reckons that countries are likely to rebuild their oil reserves only when prices returned to more reasonable levels of around US$80 per barrel.
“So, we will have a very slow rebuilding of reserves by these countries, but that implies as well that over the next two to three years oil prices will continue to be elevated.
"It might not shoot up, but it will continue to be elevated. It’s still a very fluid situation as far as fuel is concerned,” he said.
Nurhisham noted that the Suez Canal and Bab-el-Mandeb have remained open despite continuing threats.
He said the depletion of reserves would eventually remove one source of supply and that would add to uncertainty in the global energy market.

2ec059e81e766d88: PATTAYA: Thousands of US sailors aboard an aircraft carrier departed from Thailand on Sunday, AFP journalists said, concluding its first port call following reports of deteriorating living conditions on board after nine months at sea.

The 5,000-strong crew of the USS Abraham Lincoln docked just north of the resort town of Pattaya, near Bangkok, on Wednesday for five days of rest and recreation after a lengthy Middle East deployment.
Amid Thailand's tourism low season, their arrival raised hopes for businesses in Pattaya, a city known for its beaches and nightlife -- as well as its seedy reputation as a hub for sex tourism.
The Lincoln departed from the port of Laem Chabang, a half-hour drive from Pattaya, at around 11am, AFP journalists saw.
Security was stepped up in Pattaya during the visit, with authorities cracking down on sex workers ahead of the sailors' arrival -- although the mayor denied it was linked.
Despite concerns about possible trouble, local police said Sunday that the port call ended largely without incident.
"Everything went fine," Pattaya police chief Anek Srathongyoo told AFP.
"There were no arrests or arguments except on the first day when Americans had an argument among themselves," he said.
The US Navy sent two sailors back to the Lincoln after a drunken altercation in the early hours of Thursday near Pattaya's nightlife hotspot Walking Street, the police chief said earlier.
He had described the "small scuffle" as "trivial" and said local residents only called police to prevent the dispute from escalating.
Last month, US Democratic lawmakers called for an investigation into conditions on the Lincoln following reports of food shortages, broken plumbing and mental health crises.
President Donald Trump dismissed the concerns, which have fuelled criticism of his dragging war on Iran, although the Lincoln was replaced in the Middle East by the USS George Washington.
The enlisted Americans were estimated to have spent up to 100 million baht (US$3 million) during their visit, Pattaya mayor Poramase Ngampiches said on Sunday.
In addition, the city benefitted from "selling other supplies such as tootpaste to the ship worth millions of baht (tens of thousands of dollars)", Poramase told AFP.
Media reports said sailors on the Lincoln had gone without basic toiletries, including toothpaste, deodorant and soap, at points during their deployment.
Many of the sailors and Marines spent their time on Thailand's coast shopping and visiting tourism sites, Poramase said.
"It shows that they are missing their families and want to buy some souvenirs for them," he said.

bfdce3ac86d9c7bc: Kehebatan Tun M dalam politik memang tidak ada siapa yang boleh tandingi. Sama ada beliau berkuasa atau tidak, gelagat dan kata dua beliau akan sering menjadi buah mulut rakyat sekalian. Itu hebatnya Mahathir.

Beliau tidak perlu guna ayat al-Quran langsung dan tidak perlu ceramah berjela-jela dalam Facebook, cuma datang, duduk atas kerusi roda dan senyum sambil melambai. Itu pun sudah cukup untuk memulakan ribut taufan bersama halilintar.

Kenapa Tun M tak dijemput secara rasmi, 'sound' beberapa influencer yang becok berceloteh. Inikan suatu ketidakadilan kepada seorang tokoh negara? Sebenarnya saya pun agak setuju dengan teguran ini tetapi ada lima perkara yang perlu kita semua renungi dahulu.

Perkara pertama adalah apa yang disebut oleh Rafizi dalam podcastnya bila ditanya tentang isu ini. Saya berterima kasih dengan Rafizi yang memberi maklumat yang kita semua pun tak tahu. Kata Rafizi, Tun M sendiri yang mengubah protokol menjemput bekas perdana menteri untuk majlis penting seperti merdeka pada 2018.

Rafizi memberi alasan takkanlah Tun M nak duduk sebelah seorang penjenayah dan seteru beliau. Tetapi ada influencer yang tegur, Najib belum penjenayah lagi sebab baru buka kes. So, what’s the problem? Yang penting, seperti biasa, Tun memang bijak baling batu dan sembunyi tangan sambil senyum dan melambai.

Perkara kedua, kalaulah kita ada protokol untuk menjemput bekas perdana menteri atau kita ikut adab Melayu lah untuk jemput orang besar-besar, I must assume yang protokol tu dibuat dengan anggapan bahawa bekas perdana menteri tidak lagi berpolitik.

Dalam kes Tun M, beliau masih giat berpolitik dan rasanya sanggup memegang tampuk kerajaan sebagai PM untuk kali ketiga! Jadi, kalau begini rupanya, patutkah PM sedia ada menjemput seterunya dalam politik ke pentas Merdeka?

Perkara ketiga pula adalah Tun M telah membuat naratif bahawa Melayu akan hilang kuasa kalau tidak duduk di bawah satu payung besar. Sudah tentulah, payung tu dia yang punya. Jadi kalau semua Melayu duduk di situ kita boleh teka tiga kali siapa akan jadi PM.

Namun demikian, apa yang saya gusarkan adalah dengan membina naratif ini maka ia membuat suatu permusuhan dengan rakyat lain bukan Melayu termasuk Bumiputra semua. Patutkah seorang bekas PM yang menerajui negara dua kali dan masih membina naratif permusuhan antara Melayu dan bukan Melayu dijemput ke pentas duduk bersama parti PH yang tidak pernah menggunakan ras atau isu perkauman?
Saya pun tidak tergamak untuk duduk sebelah orang sebegini, tidak kisah lah dia PM berapa kali pun. Orang yang membuat kita bermusuh-musuh, bagi saya batang tubuh itu lah musuh terbesar negara kita.

Nasib baik Tun M tidak jadi seperti seorang guru agama yang nak buat kita bermusuh antara orang Islam dan bukan Islam, yang itu lagi ‘haru’ kata orang utara. Saya rasa Tun M baik sikit daripada tok guru agama yang pandai tafsir Quran ikut suka dia.

Perkara keempat adalah Tun M telah pernah membuat naratif Malaysia ini bukan negara multicultural sebab tidak ada disebutkan dalam konsep Malaysia secara undang-undang. Sekali lagi beliau memainkan isu ‘pendatang’ dan memainkan lagu lama bahawa pendatang akan take over everything kalau Melayu tak sedar dan tak bersatu. Same old song but very efective still.

Maklumlah orang Melayu ramai tidak belajar falsafah dan sejarah peradaban dunia. Kebanyakan Melayu belajar kejuruteraan, seni bina, perubatan, undang-undang dan bila pencen baru mengadap kuliah agama.

Mahathir adalah seorang pembaca tegar dan dia faham selok belok sejarah Malaysia dan dunia. Sejarah subjek kegemarannya, saya baca dalam buku beliau A Doctor in the House. Saya memang baca banyak buku Tun M, saya rasa empat buah kesemuanya. Jadi, kita kena tanya diri kita sebagai rakyat, do we want someone yang tidak admit kita negara multicultural?

Perkara kelima, memanglah dari satu sudut, kita patut jemput orang tua itu. Memang kita patut honor seorang pemimpin seperti Tun M. Tetapi jika batang tubuh itu sendiri bergerak untuk mengkucar-kacirkan kita semua, what should we do?

Pada 2016, Tun M berkempen untuk menyelamatkan Malaysia daripada perompak 1MDB. Beliau ke hulu dan ke hilir menjaja Malaysia bakal bankrap dengan si perompak ini. Bagi saya, we owe Tun M a debt of gratitude sebab dengan kempen itu kita rakyat dapat menumbangkan Umno sebagai gergasi berkuasa.

Dalam bab itu, Tun M memainkan peranan kita sebagai a united rakyat to save our country. Tetapi apabila beliau memainkan sentimen perkauman untuk menjatuhkan kerajaan perpaduan, that is an entirely different matter.

Maka itu, kita kena renung sendiri sama ada kita nak bagi hormat atau tidak kepada orang seperti Tun M. Saya sendiri amat menghormati beliau dalam banyak perkara seperti ketegasan beliau tentang ekstremis agama, tentang menimba ilmu dan memahirkan diri dalam sains, teknologi dan Bahasa Inggeris.

Tetapi saya tidak akan berkompromi kepada sesiapa pun yang cuba menjurangkan hubungan baik kita sebagai rakyat Malaysia dengan meniup bahang kaum, agama atau sejarah.That is the line I will not allow anyone to cross.
Itu jalur pemisah antara Merdeka sebagai rakyat dengan mereka yang nak menjatuhkan idea negara-bangsa kita.

a4b3f6287a5a5dbc: Saya mengikuti muktamar PAS yang sedang berlangsung di Pengkalan Chepa, Kelantan dari jauh. Ramai yang hadir dan ramai juga wakil yang berpidato dan dari situ, banyak persoalan yang timbul di benak saya.
Saya tidak banyak mendengar ucapan khusus tentang masalah negeri atau negara, apalagi tentang hal-hal yang berkait dengan ekonomi rakyat atau ekonomi negara.

Ataupun tentang hutang negara yang begitu tinggi, masalah kewangan defisit, perbelanjaan kerajaan berlebihan, Belanjawan 2027, pembahagian hasil dan pendapatan, serta bagaimana semua ini akan diuruskan sekiranya PAS mengambil alih tampuk pemerintahan negara.

Persoalan saya di sini, bukan sekadar sama ada PAS mampu memenangi pilihan raya akan datang dan membentuk kerajaan. Mereka yang hadir nampaknya percaya dan agak yakin. Sebagai contoh, 'Time for PAS to lead with its own PM candidate, says youth leader', satu impian besar yang perlu sedikit kajian dan penjelasan.
Persoalan yang lebih besar ialah: adakah PAS benar-benar mempunyai keupayaan, kepakaran dan kerangka dasar yang jelas untuk mentadbir sebuah negara majmuk?

Berapa ramai pakar ekonomi, tokoh fiskal atau kewangan, perdagangan, pendidikan, industri, pengangkutan dan pembangunan dalam PAS? Apakah mereka sekadar bergantung harap kepada rakan politiknya semata-mata?

Siapa dalam kalangan mereka yang berkaliber untuk membentuk dasar baharu? Siapakah antara yang hadir, mampu melakukan perubahan pengurusan negara supaya Malaysia bukan sekadar ditadbir, tetapi benar-benar dimajukan ke tahap yang lebih baik dan lebih tinggi?
Memerintah Malaysia bukan hanya sekadar menjadi perdana menteri, menteri atau timbalan menteri.

Ia memerlukan satu pasukan yang mempunyai kepakaran, pengalaman dan keberanian untuk membuat keputusan yang sukar, khususnya apabila berhadapan dengan masalah fiskal, hutang negara, subsidi, pelaburan, perdagangan, pendidikan, hubungan antarabangsa dan hubungan antara kerajaan persekutuan dengan Sabah dan Sarawak.
Rakyat perlu tahu apakah sebenarnya visi dan misi PAS untuk Malaysia.
Dasar fiskal
Pada pandangan saya, antara perkara paling penting yang akan menentukan kejayaan atau kegagalan mana-mana kerajaan baharu ialah dasar fiskal mereka.

Dasar fiskal ini menentukan bagaimana kerajaan memperolehi hasil, siapa yang membayar cukai, bagaimana wang dibelanjakan, siapa yang menerima bantuan dan bagaimana defisit serta hutang negara dikawal, menjadi seimbang atau ada lebihan (surplus). Di sinilah PAS perlu memberikan perhatian utama dengan pandangan yang pandai, padat dan serius.

Cadangan “Please change the movie on tax” oleh Geoffrey Williams, misalnya, merupakan satu cadangan dasar fiskal yang menarik dan wajar diberi perhatian. Tiada seorang pun yang hadir di muktamar PAS menyentuh tentang hal yang penting seperti ini.
Cadangan menggunakan electronic payment tax (EPT) sebagai mekanisme percukaian baharu, jika dilaksanakan dengan reka bentuk yang betul, berpotensi mengubah cara kerajaan mengutip hasil.

Sekiranya PAS benar-benar mahu memimpin Putrajaya, saya berpendapat mereka perlu mendengar pandangan pakar seperti beliau dan pakar-pakar dari kaum lain yang mempunyai kepakaran dalam percukaian dan kewangan awam. Persoalannya ialah: apakah model percukaian alternatif yang PAS mahu dan akan diperkenalkan?

Adakah PAS akan terus bergantung kepada sistem cukai sedia ada (SST dan GST) atau mempunyai keberanian untuk memperkenalkan pendekatan baharu yang lebih luas asasnya, lebih cekap kutipannya dan lebih adil kepada rakyat?

Jika EPT mampu direka dengan baik sehingga kutipan hasil kerajaan menjadi lebih cekap tanpa terlalu membebankan golongan berpendapatan rendah, ia boleh menjadi sebahagian daripada reset fiskal negara. Tetapi ini memerlukan kajian, kepakaran dan perancangan yang sangat teliti.

Kerajaan tetap memerlukan hasil yang mencukupi untuk membiayai kos pengurusan, belanjawan untuk pendidikan, kesihatan, keselamatan, pengangkutan awam, infrastruktur dan pembangunan negara. Justeru, PAS perlu menjelaskan bukan sahaja berapa banyak cukai yang mahu dikutip, tetapi daripada siapa, dengan cara bagaimana dan untuk membiayai apa.
Defisit, hutang dan ketirisan

Terkait dengan dasar fiskal ialah belanjawan defisit Malaysia setiap tahun yang telah melangkau lebih dua puluh lapan tahun, sejak 1998. Belanjawan defisit ini membuatkan hutang kerajaan terus meningkat, yang kini sudah melebihi RM1.38 trilion atau sejumlah 64% daripada kadar Keluaran Dalam Negara Kasar. Dalam keadaan sebegini, setiap ringgit wang negara dan wang rakyat sepatutnya diurus dengan penuh amanah, telus dan berdisiplin. Ini yang harus disahut oleh PAS.

Masalahnya bukan sekadar kerajaan berbelanja terlalu banyak. Persoalan yang lebih besar ialah ke mana wang itu dibelanjakan, berapa banyak yang benar-benar sampai kepada rakyat dan berapa banyak yang hilang akibat ketirisan, pembaziran, penyelewengan, rasuah dan salah guna kuasa.

Sebab itu, jika PAS benar-benar serius untuk mengambil alih Putrajaya, rakyat berhak menuntut satu kenyataan dan pendirian yang jelas, tegas dan tidak berkompromi mengenai rasuah dan salah guna kuasa, khususnya apabila ia melibatkan wang negara dan wang simpanan rakyat.

Tanpa kenyataan yang kukuh dan meyakinkan mengenai perkara ini, pendirian PAS boleh ditafsirkan sebagai tidak serius, lemah dan akhirnya memudaratkan negara. Apalagi di muktamar kali ini, PAS mengundang parti-parti politik yang terjebak dengan gejala rasuah dan salahguna kuasa tersebut.
Ini bukan lagi soal politik kepartian atau rakan kongsi politik. Ini soal wang negara dan wang rakyat, yang memerlukan kerangka polisi yang wajar dan kuat.

Apabila negara mempunyai hutang yang begitu besar dan terus berbelanja dalam keadaan belanjawan defisit, kerajaan tidak boleh pada masa yang sama membiarkan ruang untuk ketirisan, pembaziran dan penyelewengan terus terbuka dan berlaku.

Setiap ketirisan akhirnya perlu dibayar oleh rakyat -- sama ada melalui cukai yang lebih tinggi, pengurangan subsidi, pengurangan perkhidmatan awam, pinjaman baharu atau hutang yang akan ditanggung oleh generasi akan datang.
Oleh itu, PAS perlu menjelaskan dengan terang empat tunggak utama:

• Apakah langkah konkrit yang akan diambil untuk membanteras rasuah? • Apakah mekanisme yang akan digunapakai untuk menutup ruang ketirisan? • Apakah dasar baru yang akan diperkenalkan terhadap sistem perolehan kerajaan? • Apakah tindakan yang akan diambil terhadap mereka yang menyalahgunakan kuasa, termasuk jika mereka datang daripada parti atau gabungan politik sendiri?

Empat persoalan dan jawapan dari pihak PAS ini sangat penting. Rakyat tidak mahu mendengar janji membanteras rasuah hanya ketika PAS menjadi pembangkang. Rakyat mahu melihat apakah prinsip yang sama akan digunakan apabila PAS menjadi kerajaan dan berhadapan dengan pesalah dari orang dalam kalangan mereka sendiri atau rakan politik mereka. Yang salah, tetap salah, sama ada kawan atau lawan.

Berhubung gejala rasuah, kenyataan presiden PAS dimuktamar semalam tidak memberansangkan. Sila lihat 'Corruption in Malaysia weaponised to discredit rivals, claims Hadi'. Apakah kerajaan PAS kelak tidak akan menutup segala kebocoran dan ketirisan dalam sistem kewangan negara?
Jika kebocoran tidak ditutup, berapa banyak pun hasil yang dikutip, negara akan terus menghadapi masalah yang sama, tidak kira pesalahnya menganut agama apa sekalipun.

Ia bukan lagi isu moral semata-mata. Ia adalah isu ekonomi, isu kekuatan kewangan negara dan ianya juga, adalah isu masa depan generasi muda Malaysia. Sebab itu, isu gejala rasuah, ketirisan dan salah guna kuasa amat penting untuk dijadikan landasan sebenar polisi parti dan ia merangkumi sebahagian daripada dasar fiskal dan kewangan negara.
Jadi sebelum PAS meminta rakyat memberikan mandat untuk memimpin Putrajaya, mereka perlu terlebih dahulu menjawab satu soalan yang mudah tetapi sangat besar maknanya:
Apakah sebenarnya rancangan fiskal PAS untuk Malaysia?

3e8a758c7a64ac70: The US military's effort to prevent troops from being tracked by adversaries through purchased location data hasn't worked as well as anticipated, and lawmakers want to know why. US Senator Ron Wyden (D-OR) and Rep. Pat Harrigan (R-NC) on Friday asked for an investigation by the Defense Department Inspector General into policies that have only partially stanched the flow of location data that allows military personnel to be tracked and targeted. In May, Wyden, Harrigan, and a bipartisan group of 12 other members of Congress released details about how commercially purchased location data – often captured by mobile apps and advertising SDKs – can be used to identify where US military personnel gather and to target those locations. They noted that the DoD has been aware of this threat since at least 2016. The lawmakers urged Defense Department CIO Kirsten A. Davies to take steps to mitigate this risk, including turning off advertising identifiers on DoD smartphones and issuing a policy requiring the disabling of advertising identifiers on all personal devices brought into DoD facilities or overseas. Since then, various military branches have blocked advertising identifiers on government-issued devices. According to the letter, "several DoD components – the Army, Air Force, Navy and Marine Corps, and Special Operations Command – confirm that they now disable advertising IDs on government-issued devices to protect their personnel from such threats." But that hasn't entirely eliminated the availability of location data tied to US military personnel. Citing ongoing reports, Wyden and Harrigan want to know why location data pinpointing the movement of troops continues to be available. "We commend these service branches for implementing this cybersecurity defensive best practice on government devices," they said in their letter [PDF] to the DoD IG. "However, recent reports regarding the continued availability of commercial location data originating from DoD facilities raise troubling questions." The two lawmakers speculate about the reason DoD policies have fallen short. One possibility, they say, is that some parts of the DoD turned off their advertising identifiers only as recently as July. Another, they say, is that disabling ad identifiers may no longer be sufficient to limit the availability of location data. And the third is that the location data is coming entirely from the personal devices of DoD personnel and contractors. Zach Edwards, staff threat researcher at Infoblox, told The Register in an email that it's good to hear all the military branches have disabled advertising IDs on their phones because it will make members of the military and their families safer, especially those serving in combat zones overseas. "This change will essentially ensure that military device location data isn't being included in bulk data sales being done by numerous vendors," he said. "It’s truly unfortunate that Google and Apple have not effectively reformed their mobile advertising IDs, even after it’s been well documented that it’s the primary piece of data being used by data brokers to connect up people’s mobile phone location data for bulk sales." Mobile advertising identifiers (MAIDs), Edwards explained, serve as join keys for tracking people – they can link different datasets. "So one core benefit is that military data won't be available for sale via data brokers, who will sell to literally anyone with a pulse and a credit card," said Edwards. "But the other slightly less obvious benefit is that this MAID was also being broadcast to all ad systems participating in the auctions." Edwards said that while states like California, Vermont, Texas, and Oregon have data broker registries, he's unaware of any Russian or Chinese ad tech vendors who have registered. And those companies, he said, partner with Western publishers and mobile apps to collect data anyway. "I think it's important to appreciate that these ad tech companies in Russia and China have also likely been getting MAID data from the programmatic ad tech auctions from members of the military, and companies in those countries have an obligation to share it with the state without any ability to appeal or provide any external notice," he said. ®
